λα.def: λα insep. Prefix with intensive force, as in λά-μαχος very warlike, λα-κατάρατος much accursed.

λαασ.def: λᾶας, ου, ὁ, (a gen. λάου in Soph. as if λᾶας was of first decl.) Lat. lapis, a stone, Hom., etc.

λαβη.gloss: the part intended for grasping, a handle, haft
λαβη.def: λᾰβή, ἡ, (λαβεῖν) I. the part intended for grasping, a handle, haft, Dem.; λαβαὶ ἀμφίστομοι of a cup, Soph. II. as a pugilistic term, a grip or hold, ὥσπερ ἀθλητὴς λαβὴν ζητεῖν Plut.:—metaph. a handle, occasion, opportunity, λαβὴν διδόναι, Lat. ausam praebere, Ar.; so, λ. παραδιδόναι, παρέχειν id., Plat.

λαβραγορησ.def: λαβρ-ᾰγόρης, ου, ὁ, (ἀγορεύω) a bold, rash talker, braggart, Il.

λαβραξ.def: λάβραξ, ᾱκος, ὁ, (λάβρος) a ravenous sea-fish, perh. the bass, Ar.

λαβρευομαι.def: λαβρεύομαι, (λάβρος) Dep. to talk rashly, brag, Il.

λαβροποδησ.def: λαβρο-πόδης, ου, ὁ, (πούς) rapid of foot, rushing, Anth.

λαβροσ.def: λάβρος I. Hom. of wind, rain, etc., furious, boisterous, Hdt.; λ. πῦρ, κύματα, πόντος, etc., Eur. II. after Hom., of men, boisterous, turbulent, violent, Theogn., Soph., etc. 2. greedy, Pind., Eur. III. adv. λάβρως, violently, furiously, Theogn. 2. greedily, Aesch.

λαβυρινθοσ.def: λᾰβῠ́ρινθος, ὁ, I. a labyrinth or maze, a building consisting of halls connected by tortuous passages, Hdt. II. any spiral body, as a snail, Anth.; ἐκ σχοίνων λαβ. a bow-net of rushes, Theocr. (Origin uncertain.)

λαγαριζομαι.def: λᾰγᾰρίζομαι, Pass. to be slack or gaunt through hunger, to starve, Ar.; λᾰγᾰρόομαι, Pass. to be or become slack: of frozen water, to be in the act of thawing, Anth. (from λᾰγᾰρός)

λαγαροσ.def: λᾰγᾰρός, ή, όν 1. slack, hollow, sunken, of the flanks, Xen.:— κατὰ τὸ λαγαρώτατον in the least defensible part, Plut. 2. slack, loose, pliant, Xen.

λαγετησ.def: λᾱ-γέτης, ου, (λαός, ἁγέομαι) leader of the people, Pind.

λαγινοσ.def: λᾰ́γῐνος, η, ον of the hare, Aesch.

λαγιον.def: λάγιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λαγώς) a leveret, Xen.

λαγνεια.def: λαγνεία, ἡ, lasciviousness, lust, Xen. (from λάγνος)

λαγνοσ.def: λάγνος, η, ον lascivious, lustful, Arist.

λαγοθηρασ.def: λᾰγο-θήρας, ου, ὁ, (θηράω) a hare-hunter, Anth.

λαγυνοσ.def: λάγῡνος, ὁ, a flask, flagon, Lat. lagena, Anth., etc.

λαγχανω.gloss: to obtain by lot, by fate, by the will of the gods
λαγχανω.def: λαγχάνω (from Root ΛΑΧ) I. c.acc. to obtain by lot, by fate, by the will of the gods, Hom.; with inf. added, ἔλαχον πολιὴν ἅλα ναιέμεν I had the sea for my portion to dwell in, says Poseidon, Il.; ἔλαχ’ ἄναξ δούλην ς’ ἔχειν Eur.:—of the genius presiding over one's life, ἐμὲ μὲν Κὴρ λάχε Il.; esp. in perf. to be the tutelary deity of a place, to protect it, θεοῖσιν, οἳ Περσίδα γῆν λελόγχασι Hdt.:—absol., πρὸς Θύμβρης ἔλαχον Λύκιοι had their post assigned near Thymbra, Il. 2. of public officers, to obtain an office by lot (v. κύαμος ΙΙ); ἀρχὴν λαχεῖν, opp. to χειροτονηθῆναι (to be elected), Ar.; so, c. inf., ὁ λαχὼν πολεμαρχέειν he who had the lot to be polemarch, Hdt.; οἱ λαχόντες βουλευταί (sc. εἶναι), Oratt.; and absol., οἱ λαχόντες those on whom the lot fell, Thuc. 3. as attic law-term, λαγχάνειν δίκην to obtain leave to bring on a suit, Plat., Oratt.; and (without δίκην) λαγχάνειν τινι to bring an action against one, Oratt. II. c. gen. partit. to get one's share of, become possessed of, Hom., attic III. absol. to draw (i. e. obtain) the lot, Od.: cast lots, NTest. IV. Causal epic redupl. aor. λέλαχον, to put in possession of a thing, πυρὸς λελαχεῖν τινα to grant one the right of funeral fire, Il. V. intr. to fall to one's lot or share, Od., Eur.

λαγωδιον.def: λᾰγῴδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λαγώς,) a leveret, Ar.

λαγων.gloss: the hollow on each side below the ribs, the flank
λαγων.def: λᾰγών, όνος, (λαγαρός) I. the hollow on each side below the ribs, the flank, Eur.; in pl. the flanks, id., Ar. II. metaph. any hollow, Anth., Plut.

λαγωοσ.def: λᾰγῷος, η, ον (contr. for λαγώιος) of the hare, Ar.:— τὰ λαγῷα (sc. κρέα), hare's flesh, and, generally, dainties, delicacies, ζῆν ἐν πᾶσι λαγῴοις id. (from λᾰγῶς)

λαγωσ.def: λαγῶς a hare, Lat. lepus, Hom., Aesch., etc.

λαγωσφαγια.def: λᾰγω-σφᾰγία, ἡ, (σφαγή) a killing of hares, Anth.

λαδανον.def: λάδᾰνον, ιονιξ λήδανον, ου, τό, an aromatic gum, gum mastich, Hdt. (Foreign word.)

λαερτησ.def: λαέρτης, ου, ὁ, a kind of ant: as pr. n. the father of Ulysses, Od.; also Λαέρτιος, ου, Λάρτιος, Soph.

λαζομαι.def: λάζομαι (Dep., poetic for λαμβάνω) I. to take, seize, grasp, Il.; ὀδὰξ λαζοίατο γαῖαν may they bite the dust, id.; metaph., πάλιν δ’ ὅ γε λάζετο μῦθον he took back, i. e. altered his speech, Hom. II. the form λάζυμαι occurs in Hhymn. and Eur.

λαθητικοσ.def: λᾰθητικός, ή, όν likely to escape notice, Arist.

λαθικηδησ.def: λᾰθῐ-κηδής, ές (κῆδος) banishing care, Il., Anth.

λαθιπονοσ.def: λᾱθί-πονος, ον (λήθη) forgetful of sorrow, Soph.; βίοτος ὀδυνᾶν λ. a life forgetful of pain, id.

λαθιφθογγοσ.def: λᾰθί-φθογγος, ον robbing of voice, Hes.

λαθραιοσ.def: λαθραῖος, ον secret, covert, clandestine, furtive, Aesch., Soph.; λ. ὡδί one born in secret child-birth, Eur.:— adv. -ως, Aesch., etc.

λαθρη.def: λάθρῃ (λᾰθεῖν) 1. secretly, covertly, by stealth, treacherously, Hom.; λάθρῃ γυῖα βαρύνεται imperceptibly, Il.; so in attic, Soph., etc. 2. c. gen. without the knowledge of, unknown to, λάθρῃ Λαομέδοντος Il.; λάθρῃ τῶν στρατηγῶν Hdt.; so in attic.

λαθριδιοσ.def: λαθρῐ́διος, η, ον (poetic for λάθριος: adv. -ως, Anth.)

λαθριοσ.def: λάθριος, ον (later form of λαθραῖος, Theocr.) neut.pl. as adv., treacherously, id.

λαθροβολοσ.def: λαθρο-βόλος, ον (βάλλω) hitting secretly, δόναξ Anth.

λαθροδακνησ.def: λαθρο-δάκνης, ου, ὁ, (δάκνω) biting secretly, Anth.

λαθυροσ.def: λάθῠρος, ὁ, a kind of pulse: pl. λάθυρα Babr.

λαιγξ.def: λᾶϊγξ, γγος, ἡ, (Dim. of λᾶας) a small stone, pebble, Od.

λαιθαργοσ.def: λαίθ-αργος, ον (λᾰθεῖν) biting secretly, i. e. without barking, of a dog, Ar.

λαικαζω.def: λαικάζω, fut. άσομαι, to wench, Ar.

λαικαστησ.def: λαικαστής, οῦ, (from λαικάζω) a wencher, Ar.:—fem. λαικάστρια, a wench, harlot, id.

λαιλαψ.def: λαῖλαψ, απος, ἡ, (from λα-, λαι- intensive) a tempest, furious storm, hurricane, Hom.

λαιμα.def: λαῖμα, ατος, τό, (perh. the same as λαιμός, Ar.)

λαιμαργοσ.def: λαί-μαργος, ον very greedy, gluttonous, Arist.

λαιμοπεδη.def: λαιμο-πέδη, ἡ, I. a dog-collar, Anth. II. a springe for catching birds, id.

λαιμορυτοσ.def: λαιμό-ρῠτος, ον (ῥέω) gushing from the throat, Eur.

λαιμοσ.def: λαιμός, οῦ, the throat, gullet, Hom., Eur.

λαιμοτμητοσ.def: λαιμό-τμητος, ον (from λαιμός) (τέμνω) with the throat severed, Eur.

λαιμοτομοσ.gloss: with the throat cut, severed by the throat
λαιμοτομοσ.def: λαιμότομος, ον with the throat cut, severed by the throat, Eur.; Γοργοῦς λαιμότομοι σταλαγμοί the blood dripping from the Gorgon's severed head, id.
λαιμο-τόμος, ον (τέμνω) I. throat-cutting, Eur., Anth. II. proparox.

λαινα.def: λαῖνα, ἡ, = χλαῖνα, Lat. laena, Strab.

λαινεοσ.def: λᾱΐνεος, η, ον (= λᾱ́ϊνος, Il., Eur.)

λαινοσ.def: λᾱ́ϊνος, η, ον (λᾶας) 1. of stone or marble, Hom., etc.; λάϊνον ἕσσο χιτῶνα thou hadst put on a coat of stone, i. e. thou hadst been stoned to death, Il. 2. metaph. stony-hearted, Theocr.

λαιοσ.def: λαιός, ή, όν Lat. laevus, left, λαιᾶς χειρός on the left hand, Aesch.; πρὸς λαιᾷ χερί Eur.

λαιοτομεω.def: λαιο-τομέω, (λαῖον, τέμνω) to reap corn, Theocr.

λαισηιον.def: λαισήιον, ου, τό, (λάσιος) a kind of shield or target, lighter than the ἀσπίς, covered with raw hides, Il., Hdt.

λαιτμα.def: λαῖτμα, ατος, τό, (λαιμός) the depth or gulf of the sea, μέγα λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, ἁλὸς λ. Hom.; alone, λαῖτμα μέγ’ ἐκπερόωσι Od.

λαιφοσ.def: λαῖφος, εος, I. a tattered garment, rags, in sg. and pl., Od. II. a piece of cloth or canvas, a sail, Aesch.; in pl., Soph.

λαιψηροσ.def: λαιψηρός, ή, όν (= αἰψηρός) light, nimble, swift, Il., Pind., Eur.:—neut. pl. as adv. swiftly, Eur.

λακαζω.def: λᾰκάζω, (= λάσκω) to shout, howl, Aesch.

λακαινα.def: Λ̆άκαινα, ἡ, (fem. of Λάκων, Lat.) I. Lacaena, a Laconian woman, Theogn., etc. II. as fem. adj. = Λακωνική, Hdt., Eur., etc.

λακαταπυγων.def: λᾱκαταπῡ́γων, ον, (= καταπύγων with prefix λα-) very lascivious, Ar.

λακεδαιμων.def: Λᾰκεδαίμων, ονος, I. Lacedaemon, the capital of Laconia, and Laconia itself, Hom., Hdt., etc. II. as adj., Hdt., Eur.; but regul. adj. Λακεδαιμόνιος, α, ον, of persons, Hdt., etc.

λακερυζα.def: λᾰκέρυζα, ἡ, (from λᾰκεῖν, aor2 inf. of λάσκω) one that screams or cries, λ. κορώνη a cawing crow, Hes.; λ. κύων a yelping dog, ap. Plat.

λακισ.def: λᾰκίς, ίδος (λάσκω) a rent, rending, Aesch.; in pl., id.; λακίδες πέπλων tatters, Ar.

λακισμα.def: λάκισμα, ατος, τό, (λᾰκίζω) in pl. tatters, Eur.

λακιστοσ.def: λᾰκιστός, ή, όν (λακίζω) torn, μόρος λ. death by rending, Luc.

λακκοπλουτοσ.def: λακκό-πλουτος, ὁ, pit-wealth, Comic nickname of Callias, who found a buried treasure, Plut.

λακκοσ.def: λάκκος, ὁ, 1. a pond for water-fowl, Lat. vivarium, Hdt., Dem. 2. a pit, reservoir, Hdt., Xen.

λακτιζω.def: λακτίζω (λάξ) 1. to kick with the heel or foot, kick at, spurn, Od.; φλὸξ αἰθέρα λακτίζοισα flames lashing heaven, Pind.; κραδία φόβωι φρένα λακτίζει my heart "knocks at my ribs" for fear, Aesch.; τὸν πεσόντα λακτίσαι to trample on the fallen, id.; τὴν θύραν λ. to kick at the door, Ar.:—Pass., ὑπὸ ἵππου λακτισθείς Xen. 2. absol. to kick, struggle, of one dying, Od.: proverb., λ. πρὸς κέντρα to kick against the pricks, Pind., Aesch., etc.

λακτισμα.def: λάκτισμα, ατος, τό, a trampling on, c. gen., Aesch.; λακτιστής, οῦ, one who kicks, ἵπποι λ. kicking horses, Xen.; λ. ληνοῦ a treader of the wine-press, Anth.

λακων.def: Λᾰ́κων, ωνος, I. a Laconian or Lacedaemonian, of men, as Λάκαινα of women, Pind., Ar., etc. II. as adj. Laconian, Anth.

λακωνιζω.def: Λᾰκωνίζω, (from Λᾰ́κων) I. to imitate the Lacedaemonians, Plat., Xen., etc. II. to be in the Lacedaemonian interest, to Laconize, Xen.

λακωνικοσ.def: Λακωνικός I. Laconian, Ar., etc. II. as Subst., 1. ἡ Λακωνική (sub. γῆ), Laconia, Ar., etc. 2. Λακωνικαί (sub. ἐμβάδες), αἱ, Laconian shoes, used by men, id. 3. τὸ Λακωνικόν the state of Lacedaemon, Hdt.

λακωνισ.def: Λᾰκωνίς, ίδος (pecul. fem. of Λᾰκωνικός, Hhymn.)

λακωνισμοσ.def: Λᾰκωνισμός, οῦ, ὁ, (Λακωνίζω) I. imitation of Lacedaemonian manners, Cic. II. a being in the Lacedaemonian interest, Laconism, Xen.

λακωνιστησ.def: Λᾰκωνιστής, οῦ, (Λακωνίζω) I. one who imitates the Lacedaemonians, Plut. II. one who takes part with them, a Laconizer, Xen.

λακωνομανεω.def: Λᾰκωνο-μᾰνέω, (μαίνομαι) to have a Laconomania, Ar.

λαλαγεω.def: λᾰλᾰγέω, (λαλέω) to prattle, to babble, Pind.: of birds and grasshoppers, to chirrup, chirp, Theocr.

λαλαγημα.def: λᾰλάγημα, ατος, τό, prattle, babbling, Anth.

λαλεω.def: λαλέω (λαλός) I. to talk, chat, prattle, babble, Ar., etc.:—generally, to talk, say, Soph. 2. c. acc. to talk of, Theocr. 3. in late Gr., just like λέγω, to speak, NTest., Thuc.:—Pass., λαληθήσεταί σοι it shall be told thee, NTest. II. the proper sense, to chatter, is sometimes opp. to articulate speech, as of monkeys, λαλοῦσι μὲν φράζουσι δὲ οὔ Plut.; of locusts, to chirp, Theocr. III. of musical sounds, αὐλῶι λαλεῖν id.

λαλημα.def: λάλημα I. talk, prattle, Mosch. II. a prater, Soph., Eur.

λαλητεοσ.def: λᾰλητέος, η, ον (verb. adj. of λαλέω) to be talked of, Anth.

λαλητικοσ.def: λᾰλητικός, ή, όν (λαλέω) given to babbling, Ar.

λαλητρισ.def: λᾰλητρίς, ίδος (λαλέω) a talker, prattler, Anth.

λαλια.def: λᾰλιά, ἡ, (λαλέω) I. talking, talk, chat, Ar., Anth. 2. speech, conversation, NTest.; talkativeness, loquacity, Aeschin. II. a form of speech, dialect, NTest.

λαλιοσ.def: λαλιός, ή, όν (poetic for λάλος, Anth.)

λαλλαι.def: λάλλαι, ῶν, αἱ, (λαλέω) pebbles, from their prattling in the stream, Theocr.

λαλοεισ.def: λᾰλόεις, εσσα, εν (poetic for λᾰ́λος, Anth.)

λαλοσ.def: λᾰ́λος, ον talkative, babbling, loquacious, Eur., Plat., etc.:—metaph., λάλοι πτέρυγες Anth.:—irr. comp. λαλίστερος Ar.: Sup. λαλίστατος Eur.

λαμα.def: λαμά Hebr. words, what? why? NTest.

λαμαχιππιον.def: Λᾱμαχ-ίππιον, ου, τό, little jockey-Lamachus, Ar.

λαμαχοσ.def: Λά-μᾰχος, ον (λα-, μάχομαι) eager-for-fight, a well-known Athenian general, Ar., Thuc.

λαμβανω.def: λαμβάνω (from Root ΛΑΒ) The orig. sense of the word is two-fold, one (more active) to take, and the other (more passive) to receive I. to take: 1. to take hold of, grasp, seize, Hom., etc.; the part seized in gen., the whole in acc., τὴν πτέρυγος λάβεν caught her by the wing, Il.; γούνων λάβε κούρην Od., etc.:—then, with gen. of part only, ποδῶν, γούνων, κόρυθος λάβεν took hold of the feet, etc., Il. 2. to take by violence, seize, carry off as prize or booty, Hom. 3. λ. δίκην, ποινάς, Lat. sumere poenas, to exact punishment, Eur., etc.; v. infr. II. 3. 4. of passions, feelings, etc., to seize, Hom., etc.; of fever and sudden illnesses, to attack, Hdt., attic 5. of a deity, to seize, possess, τινά Hdt.: of darkness, and the like, to occupy, possess, Aesch. 6. to catch, come upon, overtake, as an enemy, Hom., Hdt.: to catch, find, come upon, λ. τινὰ μοῦνον Hdt., etc.: also, to catch, find out, detect, Lat. deprehendo, id.: so Pass., ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρωι εἰλημμένος caught in the act, Ar. 7. λ. τινὰ ὁρκίοισι to bind him by oaths, Hdt. 8. to take as an assistant, Soph. 9. τὴν Ἴδην λαβὼν ἐς ἀριστερὴν χέρα taking, keeping Ida to your left; so, λ. ἐν δεξιᾶι Thuc. 10. λ. Ἑλληνίδα ἐσθῆτα to assume it, Hdt. 11. to apprehend by the senses, Soph., Plat.:— to seize with the mind, apprehend, comprehend, Hdt., etc.:— to take, i. e. understand, a thing so and so, e. g. a passage of an author, Lat. accipere, Hdt., Thuc., etc. 12. to take in hand, undertake, Hdt. 13. the part. λαβών is almost pleon., as, λαβὼν κύσε χεῖρα took and kissed, Od.; so in attic II. to receive: 1. to have given one, to get, gain, win, Hom., etc.:—also in bad sense, λ. ὄνειδος Soph.; θάνατον Eur., etc. 2. to receive in marriage, Hdt., Xen. 3. λ. δίκην to receive, i. e. suffer, punishment, as we say, to catch it, Lat. dare poenas, Hdt., Eur.: —an unusual sense, v. supr. I. 2. 4. λ. ὅρκον to accept an oath as a test, Arist.; λ. λόγον to demand an account, Xen. 5. to conceive, Aesch. 6. to receive as produce or profit, Ar., Plat.; to purchase Ar. 7. to admit of, Pind. 8. of persons subject to feelings, passions, and the like, λ. θυμόν to take heart, Od.; so, periphr., λ. φόβον φοβεῖσθαι, Soph., etc.; so, λ. ὕψος ὑψοῦσθαι, Thuc.; λ. νόσον (as we say) "to take a cold, " Plat.; so, αἱ οἰκίαι ἐπάλξεις λαμβάνουσαι receiving battlements, having battlements added, Thuc. B. Mid. to take hold of, lay hold on, c. gen., σχεδίης Od., Hdt., etc. 2. of place, λ. τῶν ὀρῶν to take to the mountains, reach, gain them, Thuc.

λαμβδα.def: λάμβδα Λ, λ, λάμβδα λάβδα, τό, indecl., eleventh letter of the Gr. Alphabet: as a numeral λʹ = 30, but ͵λ = 30,000. 1. attic λ is sometimes represented by π, as κλίβανος κρίβανος, γλώσσαλγος γλώσσαργος, ναύκραρος ναύκληρος, ἀλκ-ή ἀρκ-εῖν: so, ὁλᾷς Θέωλος κόλαξ were lisping pronunc. for ὁρᾷς Θέωρος κόραξ, Ar. 2. doric λ becomes ν, as, ἦνθον φίντατος for ἦλθον φίλτατος; whereas attic λ sometimes replaces ν, as, λίτρον πλεύμων for νίτρον πνεύμων. 3. initial λ is dropt, as εἴβω for λείβω, αἰψηρὸς ἀφύσσω ἄχνη for λαιψηρὸς λαφύσσω λάχνη. 4. epic Poets double λ, metri grat., esp. after the augment, as, ἔλλαβε ἐλλιτάνευε; and in compds., as in τρίλλιστος:—and Homer omits λ, where two come together, metri grat., as Ἀχιλεύς. 5. δ sometimes becomes λ, cf. δέλτα, II. 5. 6. γ and λ are interchanged in μόγις μόλις. 7. ν before λ becomes λ, as in συλλαμβάνω ἐλλείπω.

λαμια.gloss: a monster said to feed on man's flesh, a bugbear
λαμια.def: Λάμια, ης, ἡ, (λαμός λαιμός) a monster said to feed on man's flesh, a bugbear to frighten children with, Ar.

λαμπαδαρχια.def: λαμπᾰδ-αρχία, ἡ, (ἄρχος) the superintendence of the λαμπαδηδρομία, a branch of the Gymnasiarchia, Arist.

λαμπαδηδρομια.def: λαμπᾰδη-δρομία, ἡ, (δρόμος) the torch-race, an Athenian ceremony at the festivals of the fire-gods Prometheus, Hephaestus, and Athena, in which the runners carried lighted torches, from the joint altar of these gods in the outer Cerameicus to the Acropolis; after the Persian war Pan received a like honour, Hdt.

λαμπαδιον.def: λαμπᾰ́διον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λαμπάς,) I. a small torch, Plat. II. a bandage for wounds, Ar.

λαμπασ.def: λαμπάς, άδος, (λάμπω) I. a torch, Aesch., Soph., etc.: a beacon-light, Aesch.:—later, an oil-lamp, NTest., Anth. 2. metaph. of the sun, Soph., Eur., etc.; ἡ ἐπιοῦσα λ. the coming light, i. e. the next day, Eur. II. the torch-race, like λαμπαδηδρομία, Hdt.; λαμπάδα δραμεῖν to run the race, Ar.
λαμπάς (adj., poet. fem. of λαμπρός) gleaming with torches, Soph.

λαμπεταω.def: λαμπετάω, (= λάμπω) to shine, only in epic part. λαμπετόων, shining, ὄσσε δέ οἱ πυρὶ λαμπετόωντι ἐΐκτην Hom.

λαμπη.def: λάμπη, ἡ, (= λαμπάς) a torch, Aesch.: light, id.

λαμποσ.def: Λάμπος, ὁ, one of the horses of Aurora, bright, Od.

λαμπουροσ.def: λάμπ-ουρος, ον (οὐρά) as a dog's name, firetail, Theocr.

λαμπροσ.def: λαμπρός, ή, όν (λάμπω) I. bright, brilliant, radiant, of the sun and stars, the eyes, etc., Il., attic 2. of white objects, bright, Od., Hdt. 3. of water, bright, limpid, Aesch., etc.; of the air, Eur. 4. of the voice, clear, sonorous, distinct, Lat. clarus, Dem.; so, λαμπρὰ κηρύσσειν Eur. 5. metaph. of vigorous action, λ. ἄνεμος a fresh keen wind, Hdt.; λ. καὶ μέγας καθιείς swooping down like a fresh and mighty breeze, Ar.; λαμπρὸς φανήσεται he will come vigorously forth, Eur.:—so adv., λαμπρῶς vigorously, Thuc. 6. metaph. also, clear, manifest, decisive, Aesch., Thuc.: —so adv., λαμπρῶς κοὐδὲν αἰνικτηρίως Aesch.; λελυμένων λ. τῶν σπονδῶν Thuc.; λαμπρῶς ἐλέγετο it was said without concealment, id. II. of persons, well-known, illustrious, Hdt., Dem.: also magnificent, munificent, Lat. splendidus, clarus, Dem., etc. 2. bright, joyous, Soph. III. of outward appearance, splendid, brilliant, Xen.; of youthful bloom, Thuc.: —so of dress, etc., Ar., etc.:—adv., λαμπρότατα most splendidly, Xen.

λαμπροτησ.def: λαμπρότης, ητος, (from λαμπρός) 1. brilliancy, splendour, Hdt., attic: —in pl. distinctions, Thuc. 2. splendid conduct, munificence, Dem.

λαμπροφωνια.def: λαμπροφωνία, ἡ, clearness and loudness of voice, Hdt. (from λαμπρόφωνος)

λαμπρυνω.def: λαμπρύνω (λαμπρός) I. to make bright or brilliant, Xen.:—Mid., ἐλαμπρύνοντο τὰς ἀσπίδας polished their shields, id.:— Pass., ὄμμασιν λαμπρύνεται is made clear -sighted, Aesch.; λελάμπρυνται κόρας Soph. ap. Ar.:—also to be or become clear or notorious, Eur. II. Mid. to make oneself splendid, pride oneself on a thing, distinguish oneself in, c. dat., id., Thuc.

λαμπτηρ.def: λαμπτήρ, ῆρος, (λάμπω) 1. a stand or grate for pine and other wood used for lighting rooms, Od.; ὧ χαῖρε, λ. νυκτός thou that lightest up the night, of the beacon-fire, Aesch.; ἕσπεροι λαμπτῆρες the evening watch-fires, Soph. 2. generally, = λαμπάς Eur., Xen.

λαμπτηρουχια.def: λαμπτηρ-ουχία, ἡ, (ἔχω) a holding of torches, watchfire, Aesch.

λαμπω.gloss: to give light, shine, beam, be bright, brilliant, radiant
λαμπω.def: λάμπω I. to give light, shine, beam, be bright, brilliant, radiant, of the gleam of arms, Il.; of the eyes, id.; of fire, Soph.:—Mid. or Pass., λαμπομένης κόρυθος Il., etc. 2. of sound, to be clear, ring loud and clear, Soph. 3. metaph. to shine forth, to be famous or conspicuous, Aesch., Eur., etc. 4. of persons, φαιδρὸς λάμποντι μετώπωι with beaming face, Ar.: to shine, gain glory, id. II. trans. to make to shine, light up, Eur., Anth.

λαμυρια.def: λᾰμῠρία, ἡ, audacity, impudence, Plut. (from λᾰμῠρός)

λαμυροσ.def: λᾰμῠρός, ή, όν (λαμός, λαιμός) I. gluttonous, greedy, Theocr. II. metaph. bold, wanton, impudent, Xen., Plut.

λανθανω.gloss: to escape notice, to be unknown, unseen, unnoticed
λανθανω.def: λανθάνω (from Root ΛΑΘ) A. in most of the act. tenses, to escape notice, to be unknown, unseen, unnoticed: 1. c. acc. pers., λ. τινά only, to escape his notice, Lat. latere aliquem, Hom., attic; impers., σὲ λέληθε it has escaped your notice, Plat. 2. most often with a part. added, in which case we usually translate the part. by a Verb, and express λανθάνω by an Adverb, unawares, without being observed, unseen, unknown; and this, either, a. with an acc. pers., ἄλλον τινὰ λήθω μαρνάμενος I am unseen by others while fighting, i. e. I fight unseen by them, Il.; μὴ λάθηι με προσπεσών lest he come on unseen by me, Soph. b. without an acc., μὴ διαφθαρεὶς λάθηι lest he perish without himself knowing it, id.; δουλεύων λέληθας you are a slave without knowing it, Ar.—This construct. is reversed, as in our idiom, ἀπὸ τείχεος ἆλτο λαθών (for ἔλαθεν ἁλόμενος) Il.; λήθουσά μ’ ἐξέπινες Soph. B. the compd. Verbs ἐκληθάνω, ἐπιλήθω (v. sub vocc.), take a Causal sense, to make one forget a thing, c. gen. rei: so in redupl. aor2 λέλαθον, ὄφρα λελάθηι ὀδυνάων that he may cause him to forget his pains, Il. C. Mid. and Pass. to let a thing escape one, to forget: 1. to forget, absol. or c. gen. rei, Hom.; so in redupl. aor., οὐδέ σέθεν θεοὶ λελάθοντο Il., etc.; and in perf. pass., ἐμεῖο λελασμένος id.; κείνου λελῆσθαι Soph. 2. to forget purposely, to pass over, ἢ λάθετ’ ἢ οὐκ ἐνόησεν either he chose to forget it or perceived it not, Il.

λαξ.def: λάξ with the foot, Hom., Aesch.; λὰξ πατεῖσθαι to be trodden under foot, Aesch.

λαξευτοσ.def: λαξευτός, ή, όν hewn out of the rock, NTest. (from λαξεύω)

λαξευω.def: λαξεύω, to hew in stone, Lxx.

λαξισ.def: λάξις, ιος (λᾰχεῖν) an allotment of land, Hdt.

λαοδαμασ.def: λᾱο-δ̆άμᾱς, αντος, ὁ, (δαμάω) man-taming: in Hom. as prop. name.

λαοδοκοσ.def: λαο-δόκος, ον (δέχομαι) receiving the people: in Hom. as prop. name Λαόδοκος.

λαομεδων.def: λᾱο-μέδων, οντος, ὁ, ruler of the people: in Hom. as prop. n.

λαοπαθησ.def: λᾱο-πᾰθής, ές (πάσχω) suffered by the people, Aesch.

λαοποροσ.gloss: serving as a passage for the people, man-conveying
λαοποροσ.def: λᾱο-πόρος, ον serving as a passage for the people, man-conveying, λ. μηχαναί, i. e. a bridge, Aesch.

λαοσ.def: λᾱός, οῦ, ionic ληός, attic λεώς: —, the people, both in sg. and pl., i. e. 1. in the warlike language of Il., the people or men of the army, soldiers; also a land-army, opp. to a fleet; the common men, opp. to their leaders 2. in the peaceful Od., men, people; so, ναυτικὸς λεώς seafaring folk, Aesch.; ὁ γεωργικὸς λεώς Ar.; ἀκούετε, λεῴ hear o people! the usual way of beginning proclamations at Athens, like our oyez! id. 3. in NTest. of Jews, and later of Christians, as opp. to heathens.

λαοσεβησ.def: λᾱο-σεβής, ές (σέβω) worshipped by the people, Pind.

λαοσσοοσ.def: λᾱος-σόος, ον I. （σεύω) rousing or stirring nations, Hom. 2. λαοσσόοι ἀγῶνες assemblies to which the people flock, Pind. II. （σώζω) preserving the people or nations, Anth.

λαοτινακτοσ.def: λᾱο-τίνακτος, ον stirred by a stone, Anth.

λαοτροφοσ.def: λᾱο-τρόφος, ον (τρέφω) nourishing or tending the people, Pind.; τιμὴ λ. an office useful to the people, id.

λαοτυποσ.def: λᾱο-τῠ́πος, ον (τύπτω) I. cutting stones, σμίλη Anth. II. as Subst. a stone-cutter, statuary, id.

λαοφθοροσ.def: λαοφθόρος (φθείρω) ruining the people, destructive, c. gen., Theogn.

λαοφονοσ.def: λᾱο-φόνος, ον (⁎φένω) slaying the people, Theocr.

λαοφοροσ.def: λᾱο-φόρος, λεωφόρος, ον (φέρω) bearing people, λαοφόρος ὁδός a highway, thoroughfare, Il.; ὑπὲρ τῶν μάλιστα λεωφόρων πυλέων over the gates of greatest thoroughfare, Hdt.

λαπαρα.gloss: the soft part of the body
λαπαρα.def: λᾰπ̆άρᾱ, ιονιξ -ρη, ἡ, (λαπαρός) the soft part of the body between the ribs and hip, the flank, Il., Hdt., etc.; in pl. the flanks, Lat. ilia, Hdt.

λαπαροσ.def: λᾰπᾰρός, ή, όν slack, loose, Arist.

λαπη.def: λᾰ́πη, ἡ, the scum, filth, Aesch.

λαπτω.def: λάπτω (from root ΛΑΠ) 1. to lap with the tongue, of wolves, Il. 2. to drink greedily, suck in, Luc.

λαρινοσ.def: λαρινός (λαρός) fatted, fat, Ar.; metaph., id.

λαρισα.def: Λᾱ́ρῑσα, ἡ, Larissa, a name of many old Greek cities, Il., etc.:—orig. it denoted a citadel, such as the Larissa of Argos.

λαρισαιοσ.def: Λαρισαῖος 1. Larissaean, of or from Larissa, Thuc., etc.; ionic Ληρισς- Hdt. 2. as Subst., a kind of kettle or pot, first made at Larissa, Arist.

λαρκιδιον.def: λαρκίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λάρκος, Ar.)

λαρναξ.def: λάρναξ, ακος, 1. a coffer, box, chest, Il., Hdt. 2. a cinerary urn or coffin, Il., Thuc. 3. an ark, in which children were exposed, Simon.

λαροσ.gloss: pleasant to the taste, dainty, sweet
λαροσ.def: λᾱρός, όν 1. pleasant to the taste, dainty, sweet, Hom.: —epic Sup., λᾱρώτατος οἶνος (metri grat. for λᾱρότατος) Od.: comp. λαρότερον as adv., Anth. 2. pleasant to the smell, Mosch., Anth. 3. pleasant to the eye, lovely, Anth. 4. pleasant to the ear, sweet to hear, id.
λάρος, ὁ, I. a ravenous sea-bird, perh. a cormorant, described as dashing down into the sea and then floating on the waves, Od.: metaph. of demagogues, Ar. II. a singing bird, Anth.

λαρυγγιζω.def: λᾰρυγγίζω, I. to shout lustily, bellow, bawl, Dem. II. trans. to outdo in shouting, λαρυγγιῶ τοὺς ῥήτορας Ar.

λαρυγξ.def: λᾰ́ρυγξ, υγγος, ὁ, the larynx or upper part of the windpipe, Arist.:—in Poets the throat, Eur., Ar.

λασανα.def: λᾰ́σᾰνα, τά, always in pl., a trivet or stand for a pot; also a gridiron, Ar.

λασιαυχην.def: λασιαύχην (λάσιος) with rough, shaggy neck, Hom., Ar., etc.

λασιοσ.def: λᾰ́σιος, η, ον (akin to δασύς) I. hairy, rough, shaggy, woolly, Hom., Soph., etc. II. shaggy with brushwood, bushy, Xen., Theocr.; τὰ λάσια bushes, Xen.

λασκω.def: λάσκω (from Root ΛΑΚ) I. to ring, rattle, crash, λάκε χαλκός Il.; λάκε δ’ ὀστέα the bones cracked, broke with a crash, id. II. of animals, to shriek, scream, of the falcon, ὀξὺ λεληκώς id.; of the nightingale in the falcon's talons, τί λέληκας; Hes.; also of dogs, to howl, bay, Od. III. of men, to shout, scream, cry aloud, Aesch., Soph., etc.; τί λέλᾱκας; Ar.; μή νυν λακήσηις id.:—hence of Oracles, to noise abroad, Aesch., etc.: also, to sing, πρὸς αὐλόν Eur. 2. c. acc. cogn. to shriek forth, utter aloud, Trag. IV. to crack or burst asunder, NTest.

λατομια.def: λᾱτομία, ἡ, in pl., like Lat. lautumiae, quarries, Anth.

λατρεια.gloss: the state of a hired workman, service, servitude
λατρεια.def: λατρεία, ἡ, (λατρεύω) 1. the state of a hired workman, service, servitude, Trag. 2. λ. τοῦ θεοῦ, θεῶν service to the gods, divine worship, Plat.; absol., NTest.

λατρευμα.def: λάτρευμα, ατος, τό, I. in pl. service for hire, πόνων λατρεύματα painful service, Soph. 2. service paid to the gods, worship, Eur. II. = λάτρις, a slave, id. (from λατρεύω)

λατρευω.def: λατρεύω, (λάτρις) 1. to work for hire or pay, to be in servitude, serve, Xen. 2. λ. τινί to be bound or enslaved to, Soph., Eur., etc.; c. acc. pers. to serve, Eur.:—metaph., λατρ. πέτρᾳ, of Prometheus, Aesch.; μόχθοις λατρ. Soph.; λ. νόμοις to obey, Xen. 3. to serve the gods, λ. Φοίβῳ Eur.: c. acc. cogn., πόνον λ. to render them due service, id.

λατριοσ.def: λάτριος, η, ον of a servant or service, Pind.; παραδιδόναι τινὰ λάτριον to give him into slavery, id. (from λάτρις)

λατρισ.gloss: a workman for hire, hired servant
λατρισ.def: λάτρις, ιος a workman for hire, hired servant, and in fem. a handmaid, Theogn., Soph. (from λάτρον)

λατρον.def: λάτρον, ου, τό, pay, hire, Aesch. in pl.

λαυκανιη.def: λαυκᾰνίη, ἡ, (= λαιμός) the throat, Il.

λαυρα.def: λαύρα, ιονιξ -ρη, ἡ, an alley, lane, passage, Lat. angiportus, Od., Hdt.: a sewer, drain, privy, Ar.

λαυρειον.def: Λαύρειον, ου, τό, a mountain in the S. of Attica, famous for its silver-mines, Hdt., Thuc.

λαυριωτικοσ.def: Λαυριωτικός, ή, όν of Mt. Lauri_um, Ar.

λαφυρα.def: λ̆άφῡρα, τά, (λαμβάνω) spoils taken in war, Lat. spolia, Trag., Xen.

λαφυροπωλεω.def: λᾰφῡροπωλέω, to sell booty, Xen. (from λᾰφῡροπώλης)

λαφυροπωλησ.gloss: a seller of booty, one who has bought up booty to retail
λαφυροπωλησ.def: λᾰφῡρο-πώλης, ου, ὁ, (πωλέω) a seller of booty, one who has bought up booty to retail, Lat. sector, Xen.

λαφυσσω.gloss: to swallow greedily, gulp down, devour
λαφυσσω.def: λᾰφύσσω, (λάπτω) to swallow greedily, gulp down, devour, Il.; metaph. of fire, to consume, Anth.

λαφυστιοσ.def: λᾰφύστιος, η, ον (from λᾰφύσσω) gluttonous, Hdt., Anth.

λαχαινω.def: λαχαίνω (from Root ΛΑΧΑΝ) to dig, Mosch.

λαχανισμοσ.def: λᾰχᾰνισμός, οῦ, ὁ, a gathering of vegetables, Thuc. (from λάχᾰνον)

λαχανον.def: λάχᾰνον, ου, τό, (λᾰχαίνω) 1. mostly in pl. garden-herbs, potherbs, vegetables, greens, Lat. olera, Plat., etc. 2. in pl. also, the vegetable-market, green-market, Ar.

λαχανοπωλησ.gloss: one who sells vegetables, a green-grocer;
λαχανοπωλησ.def: λᾰχᾰνο-πώλης, ου, ὁ, (πωλέω) one who sells vegetables, a green-grocer; fem. λᾰχᾰνόπωλις, ιδος, Ar.

λαχεια.def: λάχεια (λαχαίνω) fem. adj. well-tilled, fertile, Od.:—others read ἐλάχεια, from ἐλαχύς, small. (from ἐλαχύς)

λαχεσισ.def: Λάχεσις, εως (λᾰχεῖν) I. Lachesis, disposer of lots, one of the three Fates, Hes., Pind.; v. Κλωθώ. II. λάχεσις, ιος, as appellative, lot, destiny, ap. Hdt.

λαχη.def: λᾰχή, ἡ, (= λῆξις,) allotment, τάφων πατρῴων λαχαί a share in their fathers' tombs, Aesch.

λαχναιοσ.def: λαχναῖος, η, ον (= λαχνήεις, Anth.) (from λάχνη)

λαχνη.def: λάχνη, ἡ, soft hair, down, Lat. lanugo, of a young man's beard, Od., Pind.; of the thin hair on Thersites' head, Il.; of the nap or pile on cloth, id.; of sheep's wool, Soph.

λαχνηεισ.def: λαχνήεις, δοριξ -άεις, εσσα, εν (from λάχνη) hairy, shaggy, Il., Pind.

λαχνογυιοσ.def: λαχνό-γυιος, ον (γυῖον) with shaggy limbs, Eur.

λαχνοομαι.def: λαχνόομαι, Pass. to grow downy, of a youth's chin, Solon., Anth. (from λάχνος)

λαχοσ.def: λάχος (λαγχάνω) an allotted portion, Lat. sors: I. one's special lot, portion, destiny, Theogn., Soph.: one's appointed office, Aesch. II. a portion obtained by lot, a lot, share, portion, id., Xen.

λαω.def: λάω = βλέπω, to behold, look upon, c. acc., Od.; ὀξὺ λάων quick of sight, Hhymn.
λάω (an old Doric Verb, found only in pres.) (λῶ, λῆις, λῆι, λῶμες, λῆτε, λῶντι:— subj., 2 and 3rd sg. λῆις, λῆι: opt. 3rd sg. λώιη: inf. λῆν: part. τῶι λῶντι.) =θέλω, to wish, desire

λαωδησ.def: λᾱ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) popular, Lat. popularis, Plut.

λεαινα.def: λέαινα, ἡ, (fem. of λέων) a lioness, Hdt., Aesch.

λεαινω.def: λεαίνω, (λεῖος) 1. to smooth or polish, Hom.; ἵπποισι κέλευθον λειανέω I will smooth the way, Il. 2. to rub smooth, pound in a mortar, Lat. levigare, Hdt.; to grind with the teeth, Xen.:— generally, to crush, extirpate, Hdt. 3. to smooth away wrinkles, Plat.:—metaph. to smooth or soften down harsh words, Hdt.

λεαντειρα.def: λεάντειρα fem. adj. smoothing, polishing, Anth.

λεβησ.def: λέβης, ητος, (λείβω) I. a kettle or caldron of copper, Hom., etc. II. a basin in which the purifying water (χέρνιψ) was handed to the guests before meals, Od.; also a pan for washing the feet, id.: a bath, Aesch. III. a cymbal, Hdt. IV. a cinerary urn, Aesch., Soph.:—generally, a casket, Soph.

λεγεων.def: λεγεών, ῶνος, the Lat. legio, NTest., Plut.

λεγω.gloss: to lay asleep, lull to sleep
λεγω.def: λέγω (ΛΕΧ) (Pass. is only found in 3rd sg. epic aor2) part. to lay asleep, lull to sleep, λέξον με Il.; ἔλεξα Διὸς νόον id.: —Pass. and Mid. to lie asleep, to lie, Hom.

λέγω I. to gather, pick up, Lat. lego, colligo, Hom., Pind.; αἱμασιὰς λέγων picking out stones for building walls, Od.:—Mid. to gather for oneself, Il. 2. Mid. to choose for oneself, pick out, Hom.:—Pass. to be chosen, Il. II. to count, tell, reckon up, Od.; μετὰ τοῖσιν ἐλέγμην I reckoned myself among them, id.; λέκτο δ’ ἀριθμόν he told him over the number, id.:—Pass., μετὰ τοῖσιν ἐλέχθην I was counted among these, Il. 2. so in attic, λ. ἐν ἐχθροῖς to count among one's enemies, count as a foe, Aesch.; λ. τινὰ οὐδαμοῦ to count him as naught, nullo in numero habere, Soph. 3. to recount, tell over, Od., Aesch., etc.:—Mid., τί σὲ χρὴ ταῦτα λέγεσθαι; why need'st thou tell the tale thereof? Il.; μηκέτι ταῦτα λεγώμεθα id.

λέγω 1. to say, speak, Hdt., Trag., etc.; λέγε say on, Hdt.; so, λέγοις ἄν Plat.: of oracles, to say, declare, Hdt. 2. λέγειν τινά τι to say something of another, esp., κακὰ λ. τινά to speak ill of him, abuse, revile him, id.; ἀγαθὰ λ. τινά Ar.;—also, εὖ or κακῶς λ. τινά Aesch., etc. 3. to call by name, Soph.:— to call so and so, οὔτοι γυναῖκας ἀλλὰ Γοργόνας λέγω Aesch. 4. λ. τινὰ or τινὶ ποιεῖν τι to tell one to do, Soph., Xen., etc. 5. λ. τι to say something, i. e. to speak to the point or purpose, Soph.; λέγω τι; am I right? id.; opp. to οὐδὲν λέγει, has no meaning, no authority, Ar.; but οὐδὲν λέγειν, also, to say what is not, to lie, id., Plat., etc. 6. like Lat. dicere, to mean, τί τοῦτο λέγει; what does this mean? Ar., Plat.; πῶς λέγεις; how mean you? Plat.:—to explain more fully, εἴσω κομίζου σύ, Κασάνδραν λέγω get thee in—thou, I mean Cassandra, Aesch.; ποταμός Ἀχελῶιον λέγω Soph. 7. Pass., λέγεται, like Lat. dicitur, it is said, on dit, Hdt., attic; also λέγονται εἶναι they are said to be, Xen.:— τὸ λεγόμενον, absol., as the saying goes, Thuc., etc.:— ὁ λεγόμενος the so-called, οἱ λ. αὐτόνομοι εἶναι Xen. 8. of orators, to speak (emphatically), λέγειν δεινός Soph.; λ. τε καὶ πράσσειν δυνατώτατος Thuc. 9. to boast of, tell of, Xen.: to recite what is written, λαβὲ τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λέγε Plat., etc.:—but the sense of Lat. lego, to read, only occurs in compds., ἀναλέγομαι, ἐπιλέγομαι.

λεηλασια.def: λεηλασία a making of booty, robbery, Xen. (from λεηλᾰτέω)

λεηλατεω.gloss: to drive away cattle as booty, to make booty
λεηλατεω.def: λε-ηλᾰτέω, (λεία, ἐλαύνω) 1. to drive away cattle as booty, to make booty, Soph., Xen. 2. c. acc. loci, to plunder, despoil, Hdt.

λεια.def: λεία, ιονιξ ληίη, δοριξ λαία, ἡ, 1. booty, plunder, Hdt., Soph., Eur., etc.:—generally, pillageable property, Thuc., Xen.; λείαν ποιεῖσθαι χώραν λεηλατεῖν χώραν, Thuc.:— Μυσῶν λεία, of anything that may be plundered with impunity, from the effeminate character of the Mysians, Dem. 2. plunder (as an act), ζῆν ἀπὸ ληίης Hdt.

λειβω.def: λείβω (from Root ΛΙΒ) I. to pour, pour forth, οἶνον λείβειν to make a libation of wine, Hom.; also λείβειν (without οἶνον) Il.; λείβειν θεοῖς Od. II. like εἴβω, to let flow, shed, δάκρυα λ. Hom., Trag.: —Pass., of the tears, to be shed, pour forth, Eur., Xen.; of persons, λείβεσθαι δακρύοις κόρας to have one's eyes running with tears, Eur.: metaph. of sound, Pind. III. in Pass., also, to melt or pine away, Ar.

λειμαξ.def: λεῖμαξ, ακος, (= λειμών) a meadow, Eur., Anth.

λειμμα.def: λεῖμμα, ατος, τό, (= λείψανον, Plut.) τοῦ παιδὸς τὰ λείμματα what was left of him, his remains, Hdt.

λειμων.gloss: any moist, grassy place, a meadow, mead, holm
λειμων.def: λειμῶν, ῶνος, ὁ, (λείβω) any moist, grassy place, a meadow, mead, holm, Lat. pratum, Hom., Aesch., etc.

λειμωνιασ.def: λειμωνιάς, άδος, (poet. fem. of λειμώνιος, Soph.)

λειμωνιοσ.def: λειμώνιος, η, ον (λειμών) of a meadow, Lat. pratensis, Aesch., Theocr.

λειμωνοθεν.def: λειμωνόθεν (λειμών) from a meadow, Il.; also λειμωνόθε, Theocr.

λειοκυμων.def: λειο-κῡ́μων, ον, (κῦμα) having low waves, Luc.

λειομιτοσ.def: λειό-μῐτος, ον smoothing the warp, Anth.

λειοντη.def: λειοντῆ (poet. for λεοντῆ,) a lion's skin, Anth.

λειοντομαχησ.def: λειοντο-μᾰ́χης, ου, ὁ, (μάχομαι) (poetic for λεοντ-,) a lion-fighter, Theocr.

λειοντοπαλησ.def: λειοντο-πᾰ́λης, ου, ὁ, (πάλη) (poetic for λεοντ-,) a wrestler with a lion, Anth.

λειοσ.def: λεῖος, η, ον 1. Lat. levis, smooth, Il., Plat., etc.:—of cloths, smooth, plain, not embroidered, Thuc. 2. smooth, level, flat, of land, Hom.; λεῖα δ’ ἐποίησεν [θεμείλια] levelled them with the ground, Il.:—c. gen., χῶρος λεῖος πετράων smooth (i. e. free) from rocks, Od. 3. smooth-skinned, beardless, Theocr. 4. metaph. smooth, soft, of wind, Ar.; of words, Aesch.

λειοτησ.def: λειότης, ητος, smoothness, Aesch., Xen., etc.

λειπτεοσ.def: λειπτέος, ον (verb. adj. of λείπω,) one must leave or abandon, Eur., Plat., etc.

λειπω.def: λείπω (from Root ΛΙΠ) I. trans., 1. to leave, quit, Hom., etc. 2. to leave behind, leave at home, id., etc.; esp. of dying men, to leave (as a legacy), Il., etc.:— so in Mid. to leave behind one, as a memorial, Hdt., etc. 3. to leave, forsake, abandon, desert, leave in the lurch, Il., etc.; λ. ἐράνους to fail in paying.., Dem.; so, λ. δασμόν, φοράν Xen.:—conversely, λίπον ἰοὶ ἄνακτα the arrows failed him, Od. II. intr. to be gone, to be wanting, cease, be missing, Lat. deficio, Soph., Eur., etc. B. Pass. to be left, left behind, Hom., etc. 2. to remain, remain over and above, Il., Hdt., etc. 3. to remain alive, Od. II. c. gen. to be left without, to be forsaken of, σοῦ λελειμμένη Soph.;— but, λελειμμένος δορός left by the spear, i. e. not slain, Aesch. III. to be left behind in a race, Il.; λελειμμένος οἰῶν lingering behind the sheep, Od.; ἐς δίσκουρα λέλειπτο he had been left behind as much as a quoit's throw, Il.; τοῦ κήρυκος μὴ λείπεσθαι not to be behind the herald, Thuc. 2. to come short of, be inferior, worse, weaker or less than, τινος Hdt., attic; λέλειψαι τῶν ἐμῶν βουλευμάτων you come short of, understand not my plans, Eur. 3. λείπεσθαι ἀπό τινος to keep aloof from one, Il.; λ. βασιλέος or ἀπὸ βασιλέος to desert the king, Hdt.:—absol. to keep aloof, be absent, id. 4. to be wanting or lacking in a thing, ὀδυρμάτων ἐλείπετ’ οὐδέν Soph., etc.

λειριοεισ.def: λειριόεις, εσσα, εν properly, like a lily: metaph., χρὼς λειριόεις lily skin, Il.; of the cicadae, ὂψ λειριόεσσα their delicate voice, id. (from λείριον)

λειριον.def: λείριον, ου, τό, a lily, esp. the white lily, Hhymn.

λειστοσ.def: λειστός (λεώς) of or for the people, public.

λειτουργεω.gloss: to serve public offices at one's own cost
λειτουργεω.def: λειτουργέω, (λειτουργός) I. at Athens, to serve public offices at one's own cost, Oratt.; τὰ λελειτουργημένα the services performed, Dem. II. generally, to perform public duties, to serve the people or state, τῇ πόλει Xen.; so, λ. τοῖς σώμασι to serve in one's own person, Dem. III. more generally, to serve a master, c. dat., Arist. 2. to perform religious service, minister, NTest.

λειτουργημα.def: λειτούργημα, ατος, τό, the performance of a λειτουργία, Plut.

λειτουργια.def: λειτουργία, ἡ, (λειτουργέω) I. at Athens, a liturgy, i. e. a public duty, which the richer citizens discharged at their own expense.—The ordinary liturgies (ἐγκύκλιοι) were the γυμνασιαρχία, χορηγία, and ἑστίασις: the extraordinary, such as the τριηραρχία, were reserved for special occasions. II. generally, any service or ministration, help, NTest. III. the public service of the gods, Arist.:— the service or ministry of priests, NTest.: hence our word liturgy.

λειτουργοσ.def: λειτ-ουργός, οῦ, ὁ, (⁎λεῖτος, ⁎ἔργω) I. at Athens, one who performed a λειτουργία (q. v.). II. a public servant, the Roman lictor, Plut.: metaph., λ. τῆς χρείας ἐμῆς ministering to my need, NTest. III. in religious sense, a minister, id.

λειχην.def: λειχήν, ῆνος, a tree-moss, lichen, then, a lichenlike eruption, canker, scurvy, blight, Aesch.

λειχηνωρ.def: λειχ-ήνωρ, ορος, (ἀνήρ) lick-man, name of a mouse, Batr.: so also λειχο-μύλη, ἡ, Lick-meal, id.:

λειχω.def: λείχω 1. to lick up, Hdt., Aesch., Ar. 2. irreg. part. perf., γλώσσηισι λελειχμότες playing with their tongues, Hes.

λειψανον.gloss: a piece left, wreck, remnant, relic
λειψανον.def: λείψᾰνον, ου, τό, (λείπω) 1. a piece left, wreck, remnant, relic, Eur. 2. in pl., remains, remnants, Lat. reliquiae, of the dead, Soph., Plat.;—but, ἀγαθῶν ἀνδρῶν λ. are their deeds, good name, Eur.; λείψανα, remnants of youth, Ar.

λειψυδριον.def: Λειψ-ύδριον, ου, τό, (λείπομαι, ὕδωρ) a waterless district near mount Parnes in Attica, Hdt.

λειωδησ.def: λει-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) (= λεῖος,) smooth; as pr. n. in Hom.

λεκανη.def: λεκᾰ́νη, ἡ, (= λέκος, Ar.) a hod, id.

λεκανιον.def: λεκάνιον, ου, τό, Dim. of λεκᾰ́νη, Ar., Xen.

λεκιθοπωλησ.def: λεκῐθο-πώλης, ου, ὁ, (πωλέω) a peasepudding-seller, Ar.

λεκοσ.def: λέκος, εος, a dish, plate, pot, pan, Hippon.

λεκτεοσ.def: λεκτέος, η, ον (verb. adj. of λέγω) I. to be said or spoken, Plat. II. λεκτέον, one must speak, id.

λεκτικοσ.def: λεκτικός, ή, όν (λέγω) I. able to speak, Xen. II. suited for speaking, Dem.

λεκτοσ.def: λεκτός, ή, όν I. （λέγω) gathered, chosen, picked out, Aesch., Soph., etc. II. （λέγω) capable of being spoken, to be spoken, Soph., Eur., etc.

λεκτρον.def: λέκτρον, ου, τό, (λέγω) (like λέχος,) I. a couch, bed, Lat. lectus, in sg. and pl., Hom.; λέκτρονδε to bed, Od. II. pl. the marriage-bed, Pind., Trag.; ἀλλότρια, νόθα, λέκτρα, of illicit connexions, Eur.

λεληθοτωσ.def: λεληθότως (adverb from part. perf. of λανθάνω,) imperceptibly, Plat.

λελιημαι.def: λελίημαι (λίαν) to strive eagerly, in part. λελῐημένος, Il.; as a mere adj. eager, in haste, id.: later 3rd sg. plup., Theocr.

λελογισμενωσ.def: λελογισμένως according to calculation, Hdt., Eur.

λεμβοσ.def: λέμβος, ὁ, I. a boat, Lat. lembus, a ship's cock-boat, Dem. II. a fishing-boat, Theocr.

λεμμα.gloss: that which is peeled off, peel, husk, skin, scale
λεμμα.def: λέμμα, ατος, τό, (λέπω) that which is peeled off, peel, husk, skin, scale, Ar.

λεντιον.def: λέντιον, ου, τό, Lat. linteum, a cloth, napkin, NTest.

λεξισ.def: λέξις, εως (λέγω) I. a speaking, saying, speech, Plat. 2. a way of speaking, diction, style, id., etc. II. κατὰ λέξιν as the phrase goes, Anth.

λεοντεη.def: λεοντέη (poet. λειοντῆ) (sub. δορά) a lion's skin, Hdt., Ar. (from λεόντεος)

λεοντεοσ.def: λεόντεος, ποετ. λεόντειος, η, ον of a lion, Theocr.

λεοντοβοτοσ.def: λεοντό-βοτος, ον (βόσκω) fed on by lions, Strab.

λεοντοδιφροσ.def: λεοντό-διφρος, ον in chariot drawn by lions, Anth.

λεοντοφοροσ.gloss: bearing the figure of a lion
λεοντοφοροσ.def: λεοντο-φόρος, ον bearing the figure of a lion, Luc.

λεοντοφυησ.def: λεοντο-φυής, ές (φυή) of lion nature, Eur.

λεοντοχλαινοσ.def: λεοντό-χλαινος, ον (χλαῖνα) clad in a lion's skin, Anth.

λεπαδνον.def: λέπαδνον, ου, τό, a broad leather strap fastening the yoke (ζυγόν) to the neck, and passing between the fore-legs to the girth (μασχαλιστήρ), mostly in pl., Il., Aesch.: so metaph., ἀνάγκης δῦναι λέπαδνον to put on the halter of necessity, Aesch.

λεπαιοσ.def: λεπαῖος, η, ον (λέπας) rocky, rugged, Eur.

λεπαργοσ.def: λέπ-αργος, ον (λέπος) with white coat, Theocr.

λεπασ.def: λεπάς, άδος, a limpet, from its clinging to the rock (λέπας), Ar.
λέπας (only in nom. and acc.) (λέπω) a bare rock, scaur, crag, Aesch., Eur., etc.

λεπαστη.def: λεπαστή, ἡ, (from λεπάς) a limpet-shaped drinking-cup, Ar.

λεπιδοομαι.def: λεπῐδόομαι, (λεπίς) Pass. to be covered with scales.

λεπιδωτοσ.def: λεπῐδωτός, ή, όν I. scaly, covered with scales, of the crocodile, Hdt.; of scale-armour, id. II. as Subst., a fish of the Nile with large scales, id.

λεπισ.def: λεπίς, ίδος (λέπω) 1. a scale, husk, λ. ᾠοῦ an egg- shell, Ar.; the cup of a filbert, Anth. 2. collectively, the scales of fish, Hdt.

λεπρασ.def: λεπράς, άδος, (poet. fem. of λεπρός, Theocr.)

λεπροσ.def: λεπρός, ή, όν (λέπω) scaly, scabby, rough, leprous, Ar.

λεπτακινοσ.def: λεπτᾰκῐνός, ή, όν (poetic for λεπτᾰλέος, Anth.)

λεπταλεοσ.def: λεπτᾰλέος, η, ον (λεπτός) fine, delicate, Il., Anth.

λεπτεπιλεπτοσ.def: λεπτ-επί-λεπτος, ον thin-upon-thin, i. e. thin as thin can be, Anth.

λεπτογειοσ.def: λεπτό-γειος, ον (γαῖα, γῆ) of thin, poor soil, Thuc.

λεπτογραμμοσ.def: λεπτό-γραμμος, ον (γράμμα) written small or neat, Luc.

λεπτογραφοσ.def: λεπτό-γρᾰφος, ον (γράφω) written small or neat, Luc.

λεπτοδομοσ.def: λεπτό-δομος, ον (δέμω) slightly framed, slight, Aesch.

λεπτολογεω.gloss: to talk subtly, to chop logic, quibble
λεπτολογεω.def: λεπτολογέω, to talk subtly, to chop logic, quibble, Ar.; λ. τι to discuss in quibbling fashion, Luc.:—so as Dep. λεπτολογέομαι, id. (from λεπτολόγος)

λεπτολογοσ.def: λεπτο-λόγος, ον (λέγω) speaking subtly, subtle, quibbling, Ar.

λεπτομιτοσ.def: λεπτό-μῐτος, ον of fine threads, Eur., Anth.

λεπτον.gloss: a very small coin, a mite
λεπτον.def: λεπτόν sc. νόμισμα a very small coin, a mite, NTest.

λεπτοσ.def: λεπτός, ή, όν (λέπω) I. peeled, husked, threshed out, Il. 2. fine, small, of dust, ashes, etc., id., Soph., Ar. 3. thin, fine, delicate, of cloth, thread, etc., Hom., Eur. 4. of the human figure, thin, lean, meagre, Ar., Xen.: also slender, taper, Plat. 5. of space, like στενός, strait, narrow, Od.; ἐπὶ λεπτόν in a thin line, Xen. 6. generally, small, weak, impotent, μῆτις Il.; ἐλπίς Ar.; λ. ἴχνη faint traces, Xen.; τὰ λεπτὰ τῶν προβάτων small cattle, i. e. sheep and goats, Hdt.; λ. πλοῖα small craft, id., etc. 7. light, slight, of sounds, Aesch.; λ. πνοαί light breezes, Eur. 8. of wine, light, Luc. II. metaph. fine, subtle, refined, νοῦς, μῦθος Eur., etc.:— so adv., λεπτῶς μεριμνᾶν Plat.

λεπτοτησ.def: λεπτότης, ητος, (λεπτός) 1. thinness: fineness, delicacy, leanness, Plat. 2. metaph. subtlety, Ar.

λεπτοτομεω.def: λεπτο-τομέω, (τέμνω) to cut small, mince, Strab.

λεπτουργεω.def: λεπτουργέω, 1. to do fine work, of joiners and turners, Plut. 2. metaph. = λεπτολογέω, Eur.

λεπτυνω.def: λεπτύνω (λεπτός) to make small or fine: to thresh out, winnow, Anth.:—Pass. to be reduced, grow lean, Arist.; τοὺς ὤμους λεπτύνεσθαι Xen.

λεπυριον.def: λεπῡ́ριον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λέπυρον, Theocr.)

λεπυριωδησ.def: λεπῡρι-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) consisting of coats or layers, like the onion, Arist.

λεπυρον.def: λέπῡρον, ου, τό, (λέπω) a shell, husk, rind.

λεπω.def: λέπω I. to strip off the rind or husks, to peel, bark, περὶ γάρ ῥά ἑ χαλκὸς ἔλεψεν φύλλα τε καὶ φλοιόν Il. II. metaph. in Com. poets, to hide, i. e. thrash.

λερνα.def: Λέρνα, ἡ, Lerna, in Argolis, the abode of the Hydra, Eur.:—adj. Λερναῖος, η, ον or ος, ον, Hes., Eur.

λεσβιαζω.def: Λεσβιάζω, to imitate Sappho (the Lesbian poetry), Ar. (from λέσβιος)

λεσβιοσ.def: λέσβιος, η, ον Lesbian, of Lesbos, Hdt., etc.

λεσβισ.def: Λεσβίς, ίδος a Lesbian woman, Il.; so Λεσβιάς, άδος, Anth.

λεσβοσ.def: Λέσβος, ἡ, Lesbos, an island on the W. coast of Asia Minor, Hom., etc.

λεσχαζω.def: λεσχάζω, to prate, chatter, Theogn. (from λέσχη)

λεσχη.gloss: a place where people assembled to talk and hear news, a lounge, club-room
λεσχη.def: λέσχη, ἡ, (λέγω) I. a place where people assembled to talk and hear news, a lounge, club-room, Od., etc.: —also a council-hall, council, Aesch., Soph. II. talk or gossip, such as went on in the λέσχαι, Eur.:— in good sense, conversation, discussion, Hdt., Soph.

λεσχηνευω.def: λεσχηνεύω, (λέσχη) to chat or converse with, τινί App.; in Mid. to chat, converse, cf. προ-λεσχηνεύομαι.

λευγαλεοσ.def: λευγᾰλέος, η, ον (akin to λυγρός) in sad or sorry plight, wretched, pitiful, dismal, Od.:—adv., so, λευγαλέως χωρεῖν to go in ill plight, Il.

λευιτησ.def: Λευίτης, ου, ὁ, (Λευί, Levi) a Levite, NTest.

λευκαινω.def: λευκαίνω, (λευκός) 1. to make white, whiten, Od., Eur., etc. 2. to make bright or light, ἠὼς λευκαίνει φῶς morn brightens up her light, Eur.

λευκανθησ.def: λευκ-ανθής, ές (ἀνθέω) white-blossoming; generally, blanched, white, Pind.; v. χνοάζω.

λευκανθιζω.def: λευκανθίζω, (from λευκανθής) to have white blossoms: generally, to be white or made white, Hdt., Babr.

λευκαργιλοσ.def: λευκάργῑλος, ον of or with white clay, Strab.

λευκασ.def: λευκάς, άδος, I. poet. fem. of λευκός, Eur.

λευκασπισ.def: λεύκ-ασπις, ῐδος, ὁ, ἡ, white-shielded, Il., Xen.:—in Trag. the Argives are λευκάσπιδες.

λευκη.def: λεύκη, ἡ, (λευκός) I. white leprosy, Hdt., etc. II. the white poplar, Lat. populus alba, Ar., Dem.

λευκηρετμοσ.def: λευκ-ήρετμος, ον (ἐρετμός) with white oars, Eur.

λευκιππιδεσ.def: Λευκιππίδες daughters of Leucippus, nymphs worshipped at Sparta, Eur.

λευκιπποσ.def: λεύκ-ιππος, ον riding or driving white horses, Pind., Soph.; λ. ἀγυιαί streets thronged with white horses, Pind.

λευκογραφεω.def: λευκο-γρᾰφέω, (γράφω) to paint in white on a coloured ground, Arist.

λευκοθεα.def: Λευκοθέα, ἡ, the white goddess, under which name Ino was worshipped as a sea-goddess, Od.

λευκοθριξ.def: λευκό-θριξ, τρῖχος, ὁ, ἡ, λευκότρῐχος, ον, white-haired, white, Eur., Ar.

λευκοθωραξ.def: λευκο-θῶραξ, ᾱκος, ὁ, ἡ, with white cuirass, Xen.

λευκοινοσ.def: λευκόῐ̈νος, η, ον made of λευκόϊον, Anth.

λευκοιον.def: λευκό-ϊον, ου, τό, for λευκὸν ἴον, literally white-violet, but used for I. the wall-flower, Theocr., etc. II. a bulbous plant, the snow-flake, Anth.

λευκοκυμων.def: λεῡκο-κύμων, ον, (κῦμα) white with surf, Eur.

λευκολινον.def: λευκό-λῐνον, ου, τό, white flax for ropes and rigging, Hdt.

λευκολοφοσ.def: λευκό-λοφος, ον white-crested, Ar.:—as Subst. λευκόλοφον, τό, a white hill, Anth.

λευκον.def: λευκόν, οῦ, 1. white, as a colour, τὸ λ. οἶδεν knows black from white, Ar. 2. a white dress, λευκὸν ἀμπέχει are dressed in white, id.

λευκοοπωροσ.def: λευκο-όπωρος, ον (ὀπώρα) with white fruit, Anth.

λευκοπετρον.def: λευκό-πετρον, ου, τό, (πέτρα) a white rock, Polyb.

λευκοπηχυσ.def: λευκό-πηχυς, υ, gen. εως, white-armed, Eur.

λευκοπτεροσ.def: λευκό-πτερος, ον (πτερόν) white-winged, of a ship, Eur.:—generally, white, Aesch., Eur.

λευκοπωλοσ.def: λευκό-πωλος, ον with white horses, Trag.

λευκοσ.def: λευκός, ή, όν (from Root ΛΥΚ) I. light, bright, brilliant, of sun light, Hom., Soph.; and of metallic surfaces, λέβης Il.; also, λ. γαλήνη a glassy calm, Od.; of water, generally, bright, limpid, Hom., Eur. 2. metaph. clear, plain, distinct, of authors, Anth. II. of colour, white, Hom., etc.; λ. ἅρμα λεύκιππον, Eur. 2. of the skin, white, fair, Hom., Trag.; with a notion of bare, πούς Eur., cf. λευκόπους:—later, as a mark of effeminacy, blanched, white, pale, Ar., Xen.:— λευκαὶ φρένες in Pind. may be pale with envy, envious. 3. λ. χρυσός, pale gold, i. e. gold alloyed with silver (prob. the same as ἤλεκτρον), opp. to χρυσὸς ἄπεφθος, Hdt. 4. λευκὸν ἦμαρ νυκτὸς ἐκ μελαγχίμου a bright day after a night of mourning, Aesch.

λευκοφρυσ.def: λεύκ-οφρυς, υ, white-browed, Orac. ap. Hdt.

λευκοχρουσ.def: λευκό-χρους, ουν (χρόα) of white complexion: heterocl. acc. λευκόχροα κόμαν Eur.

λευκοω.def: λευκόω, (λευκός) to make white: λ. πόδα to bare the foot, Anth.:—Mid., λευκοῦσθαι τὰ ὅπλα to whiten their shields, Xen.:—Pass. to be or become white, Pind.

λευκωμα.def: λεύκωμα, ατος, τό, (λευκόω) a tablet covered with gypsum to write on, a notice-board, register, Lat. album, Oratt.

λευροσ.def: λευρός, ή, όν (λεῖος) 1. smooth, level, even, Od., Aesch., Eur. 2. smooth, polished, Pind.

λευσιμοσ.def: λεύσῐμος, ον (λεύω) stoning, Eur.; λ. καταφθοραί or θάνατος death by stoning, id.; λ. ἀραί curses that will end in stoning, Aesch.

λευσσω.def: λεύσσω, 1. to look or gaze upon, see, behold, Il., Trag. 2. absol. to look, gaze, Hom., Soph., etc.:— ὁ μὴ λεύσσων he that sees no more, i. e. is dead, Soph.; so, εἰ λεύσσει φάος if he still sees the light, Eur. 3. c. acc. cogn., λεύσσειν δέργμα δράκοντος to look the look of a dragon, Aesch.; λ. φόνον to look murder, Theocr.

λευστηρ.def: λευστήρ, ῆρος, (λεύω) I. one who stones, a stoner, Eur.: —in Orac. ap. Hdt., λευστήρ is prob. one deserving to be stoned. II. as adj., λευστὴρ μόρος death by stoning, Aesch.

λευω.def: λεύω (λᾶας) to stone, Thuc., Eur.:—Pass., λευσθῆναι πέτροις Soph.

λεχαιοσ.def: λεχαῖος, η, ον (λέχος) in bed, τέκνα λεχαῖα nestlings, Aesch.

λεχεποιη.gloss: grown with grass fit to make a bed
λεχεποιη.def: λεχε-ποίη, ἡ, (λέχος, ποία) grown with grass fit to make a bed, i. e. grassy, meadowy, Il., Hhymn.

λεχεποιησ.def: λεχεποίης, ου, (masc. of λεχεποίη) of the river Asopus, from its grassy banks, Il., Orac. ap. Hdt.

λεχοσ.def: λέχος, εος, (λέγω) 1. a couch, bed, Hom., etc. 2. a kind of state-bed or bier, Il., etc. 3. a marriage-bed, and generally marriage, Od., Trag.; so in pl. τὰ νυμφικὰ λ. Soph.; γῆμαι μείζω λέχη to make a great marriage, Eur., etc.:—also for the concrete, σὰ λέχεα thy spouse, id. 4. a bird's nest, Aesch., Soph.

λεχριοσ.def: λέχριος, η, ον slanting, slantwise, crosswise, Lat. obliquus, Soph., Eur.:—metaph., πάντα γὰρ λ. τἀν χεροῖν all the business in hand is cross, Soph. (from λέχρῐς)

λεχω.def: λεχώ (λέχος) a woman in childbed, or one who has just given birth, Lat. puerpera, Eur.

λεχωιοσ.def: λεχώιος, ον (from λεχώ) of or belonging to child-bed, δῶρα λεχ. presents made at the birth, Anth.

λεωκοριον.gloss: the temple of the daughters of Leos
λεωκοριον.def: Λεω-κόριον, ου, τό, (κόρη) the temple of the daughters of Leos, Thuc.

λεων.def: λέων, οντος, ὁ, 1. Lat. leo, a lion, Hom.; of Artemis, Ζεύς σε λέοντα γυναιξὶ θῆκε Zeus made thee a lion toward women, because she was supposed to cause their sudden death, Il.; οἴκοι λέοντες, ἐν μάχῃ δ’ ἀλώπεκες Ar. 2. = λεοντῆ, a lion's skin, Luc.

λεωργοσ.def: λε-ωργός, όν (adv. λέως, Ἔργω) one who will do anything, i. e. audacious, villainous, a knave, Aesch.; λεωργότατος Xen.

λεωσ.def: λέως (ionic adv. = λίαν) entirely, wholly, λ. οὐδέν nothing at all, Archil.; cf. λεωργός.

λεωσφετεροσ.gloss: one of their own people, a fellow-citizen
λεωσφετεροσ.def: λεω-σφέτερος, ον one of their own people, a fellow-citizen, Hdt.

ληγω.def: λήγω I. to stay, abate, like παύω, Il.:—c. gen., χεῖρας λήγειν φόνοιο to stay hands from murder, Od. II. intr. to leave off, cease, come to an end, Il., Hdt., attic: c. gen. to stop or cease from a thing, χόλοιο, φόνοιο, etc., Il., attic: c. part to cease doing, λήγειν ἀείδων Il., etc.

ληδαριον.def: λῃδᾰ́ριον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λῇδος, Ar.)

ληδον.def: λῆδον, ου, τό, a shrub, the mastich, on which the gum λάδανον is found, cistus creticus.

ληδοσ.def: λῆδος, δοριξ λᾷδος, εος, a light summer dress, Alcman.

ληθαιοσ.def: λήθαιος, ληθαῖος, η, ον (Λήθη) of or from Lethe, Lethean, Anth.

ληθαργικοσ.def: ληθαργικός, ή, όν drowsy, Anth. (from λήθαργος)

ληθαργοσ.def: λήθ-αργος, ον (λήθη) I. forgetful: c. gen. forgetful of, Anth., II. as Subst. lethargy, Arist.

ληθεδανοσ.def: ληθεδᾰνός, ή, όν (λήθη) causing forgetfulness, Luc.

ληθη.def: λήθη, δοριξ λάθα, ἡ, (λανθάνω) I. a forgetting, forgetfulness, Lat. oblivio, Il., attic; λ. παρέχειν, ἐμποιεῖν Plat.; εἰς λήθην ἐμβάλλειν τινά Aeschin., etc. II. after Hom., a place of oblivion in the lower world, Simon., etc.

ληιασ.def: ληιάς (poet. fem. of ληίδιος) taken prisoner, captive, Il.

ληιβοτηρ.def: ληι-βοτήρ, ῆρος, (λήιον) crop-consuming, crop destroying: fem., σῦς ληιβότειρα, Od.

ληιδιοσ.def: ληίδιος, η, ον (ληίς) taken as booty, captive, Anth.

ληιζομαι.gloss: to seize as booty, to carry off as prey
ληιζομαι.def: ληίζομαι, (ληίς) Dep.: I. to seize as booty, to carry off as prey, Hom., Hdt.:—generally, to get by force, to gain, get, Hes. 2. to plunder, despoil, esp. by raids or forays, ἀλλήλους Thuc., Xen. 3. absol. to plunder, Hdt. II. perf. λέλῃσμαι in pass. sense, to be carried off, taken as booty, Eur.

ληινομοσ.def: ληι-νόμος, ον (νέμω) dwelling in the country, Anth.

ληιον.def: λήιον, δοριξ λαῖον, ου, τό, 1. a crop, Lat. seges, ὡς δ’ ὅτε κινήσῃ Ζέφυρος βαθὺ λήιον Il.; so Hes., Hdt. 2. a corn-field, field, Theocr., Babr.

ληισ.def: ληίς, δοριξ λᾱίς, ίδος (epic for λεία,) booty, spoil, Hom., etc.; mostly of cattle, Il.; and without notion of plunder, cattle, stock, Hes., Theocr.

ληιστηρ.def: ληιστήρ, ῆρος, (epic form of λῃστής,) a robber, esp. a pirate, rover, Od.

ληιστησ.def: ληιστής, οῦ, (= attic λῃστής, Hhymn., Hdt.)

ληιστοσ.gloss: to be carried off as booty, to be won by force
ληιστοσ.def: ληιστός, ή, όν to be carried off as booty, to be won by force, Il.; also (with the vowel shortd.) λεϊστός id.

ληιστυσ.def: ληιστύς, ύος plundering, ionic form in Hdt.

ληιστωρ.def: ληίστωρ, ορος, I. = ληιστήρ, Od. II. as adj. plundering, Anth.

ληιτισ.def: ληῖτις (ληίς) she who makes or dispenses booty, Il.

ληιτον.def: λήιτον, ου, τό, (λαός, λεώς) Achaean name for the town-hall or council-room, = Athen. πρυτανεῖον, Hdt., Plut.

ληκεω.def: ληκέω, doric λᾱκέω, to sound, Theocr.

ληκυθιζω.def: ληκῠθίζω, (λήκυθος II) to adorn rhetorically, amplify, Strab.

ληκυθιον.def: ληκῠ́θιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λήκυθος,) a small oil-flask, Ar.

ληκυθοσ.def: λήκῠθος, ἡ, I. an oil-flask, oil-bottle, Od., Ar.: a casket for unguents, Ar. II. in pl. tropes, tragic phrases, Lat. ampullae, Cicero. (deriv. uncertain)

λημα.def: λῆμα, ατος, τό, (λάω) I. will, desire, resolve, purpose, mind, Aesch., Eur. II. temper of mind, spirit, whether, 1. good, courage, resolution, Hdt., Pind., attic; or, 2. bad, insolence, arrogance, audacity, Soph.

ληματιαω.def: λημᾰτιάω, (λῆμα) to be high-spirited, resolute, Ar. (only in pres.)

λημαω.def: λημάω, to be blear-eyed or purblind, λημᾶν κολοκύνταις to have one's eyes running pumpkins, Ar.: metaph., λημᾶν τὰς φρένας id. (only in pres.) (from λήμη)

λημη.gloss: a humour that gathers in the corner of the eye, gum, rheum
λημη.def: λήμη, ἡ, a humour that gathers in the corner of the eye, gum, rheum:—metaph., Pericles called Aegina ἡ τοῦ Πειραιέως λ. the eyesore of Peiraeeus, Arist., Plut.; λῆμαι Κρονικαί old prejudices that dim the eyes, Ar.

λημμα.def: λῆμμα, ατος, τό, (εἴλημμαι, perf. pass. of λαμβάνω) anything received, income, Aesch.; λ. καὶ ἀνάλωμα receipt and expense, Plat.: generally, gain, profit, Lat. lucrum, Soph., etc.; παντὸς ἥττων λήμματος unable to resist any temptation of gain, Dem.; often in pl., id.

λημνιοσ.def: Λήμνιος, η, ον Lemnian, v. Λῆμνος.

λημνισκοσ.def: λημνίσκος, ὁ, (λῆνος) a woollen fillet or riband, Lat. taenia, Plut., etc.

λημνοσ.def: Λῆμνος, ἡ, Lemnos, an island in the Aegaean sea, sacred to Hephaestus, Hom., etc.:—from the volcanic nature of the island, the Λήμνιον πῦρ became proverbial, Soph.

ληναικοσ.def: Ληναϊκός, ή, όν of or belonging to the Λήναια, Anth.

ληναιοσ.def: ληναῖος, η, ον (ληνός) belonging to the wine-press: 1. epith. of Bacchus as god of the wine-press, Diod. 2. Λήναια (sc. ἱερά), τά, the Lenaea, an Athenian festival held in the month Ληναιών in honour of Bacchus, at which there were contests of the Comic Poets, Ar. 3. Λήναιον, ου, τό, the Lenaeum, or place at Athens where the Lenaea were held, id., Plat.

ληναιων.def: Ληναιών, ῶνος, ionic name of the seventh attic month ὁ, Γαμηλιών, in which the Lenaea were held (v. Διονύσια) the latter part of Jan. and former of Feb., Hes.

ληνοσ.def: ληνός, δοριξ λᾱνός, οῦ, like Lat. lacus, alveus, a tub or trough; esp., 1. a wine-vat, Theocr. 2. a trough for watering cattle, Hhymn.
λῆνος, εος, Lat. lana, wool, Aesch.

ληξιαρχικοσ.def: ληξιαρχικός, ή, όν belonging to the ληξίαρχος·—τὸ λ. γραμματεῖον the register of each Athenian deme, Dem. (from ληξίαρχος)

ληξιαρχοσ.def: ληξί-αρχος, ὁ, the officer at Athens who entered young citizens on the list of their deme when they came of age.

ληξισ.gloss: a portion assigned by lot, an allotment
ληξισ.def: λῆξις (λήχομαι, fut. of λαγχάνω) I. a portion assigned by lot, an allotment, Plat.; cf. λάξις. II. as law-term, λ. δίκης or λ. alone, a written complaint lodged with the Archon, as the first step to a lawsuit, id., Aeschin.

ληπτεοσ.def: ληπτέος, η, ον (verb. adj. of λαμβάνω,) I. to be taken or accepted, Plat. II. neut. ληπτέον, one must take hold, Ar.: one must undertake, Xen.; one must take or choose, id. 2. one must take, receive, id.

ληπτικοσ.def: ληπτικός, ή, όν (λαμβάνω) disposed to accept, Arist.

ληπτοσ.def: ληπτός, ή, όν (verb. adj. of λαμβάνω,) to be apprehended, Plat., Anth.

ληρεω.def: ληρέω (λῆρος) to be foolish or silly, speak or act foolishly, Lat. nugari, Soph., Ar.

ληρημα.def: λήρημα, ατος, τό, (from ληρέω) silly talk, nonsense, Plat.

ληροσ.def: λῆρος, ὁ, silly talk, nonsense, trumpery, Ar.:—of persons, nonsense, a trifler, Plat.; λῆροι λεπτότατοι, of sophists, Ar.; as an exclamation, λῆρος, nonsense! humbug! id.
ληρός, οῦ, ὁ, a poor trinket, Anth.

ληρωδησ.def: ληρ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) frivolous, silly, Plat., Arist.

λησιμβροτοσ.def: λησί-μβροτος, ον (λήθω, βροτός) taking men unawares, a thief, Hhymn.

λησμοσυνη.def: λησμοσύνη, ἡ, (= λήθη) forgetfulness, Hes., Soph.

λησταρχησ.def: λῃστ-άρχης, ου, ὁ, (ἄρχω) a captain of robbers, Plut.

ληστεια.gloss: a robber's life, robbery, piracy, buccaneering
ληστεια.def: λῃστεία, ἡ, a robber's life, robbery, piracy, buccaneering, Lat. latrocinium, Thuc., Xen. (from λῃστεύω)

ληστευω.gloss: to be a robber: to carry on a piratical
ληστευω.def: λῃστεύω, (λῃστής) 1. to be a robber: to carry on a piratical war, to practise piracy, Lat. latrocinari, Dem. 2. c. acc. to spoil, plunder, Thuc.

ληστηριον.def: λῃστήριον, ου, τό, I. a band of robbers, Xen., Aeschin.:— a retreat or nest of robbers, Strab. II. robbery, in pl., Luc. (from λῃστής)

ληστησ.def: λῃστής, οῦ, (ληίζομαι) a robber, plunderer, Soph., Eur., Xen.; esp. by sea, a pirate, rover, buccaneer, Hdt., Thuc., etc.

ληστικοσ.def: λῃστικός, ή, όν 1. inclined to rob, piratical, buccaneering, Thuc., Dem.:— τὸ λῃστικόν piracy, Thuc.; also a band of robbers, id. 2. adv. -κῶς, in the manner of pirates; comp. -κώτερον, id.

ληστισ.def: λῆστις, ιος (only in nom. and acc.) (= λήθη, Eur.) λῆστιν ἴσχειν ἐπιλανθάνεσθαι, to forget, Soph.

ληστρικοσ.def: λῃστρικός, ή, όν (= λῃστικός) piratical, Thuc., etc.

ληστρισ.def: λῃστρίς, ίδος (pecul. fem. of λῃστρικός) ναῦς λ. a pirate vessel, Dem., etc.

λητογενησ.def: Λητο-γενής, δοριξ Λᾱτο-γενής, ές (γίγνομαι) born of Leto, epith. of Apollo and Artemis, Eur.: pecul. fem. Λατογένεια, Aesch.

λητοιδησ.def: Λητοῐ̈́δης, δοριξ Λᾱτοΐδας, ου, ὁ, son of Leto, i. e. Apollo, Hhymn., Hes.

λητω.def: Λητώ Leto, Lat. Latona, mother of Apollo and Artemis, Hom.

λητωοσ.def: Λητῷος, η, ον (from Λητώ) of or born from Leto, Soph.; doric Λατῴα, Anth.: fem. also Λητωίς, ίδος, id.

ληψισ.gloss: a taking hold, seizing, catching, seizure
ληψισ.def: λῆψις, εως (λήψομαι) 1. a taking hold, seizing, catching, seizure, Thuc. 2. an accepting, receiving, Plat.; in pl. receipts, id.

λιαζομαι.def: λιάζομαι (= κλίνω) epic Dep to bend, incline: I. mostly of persons, to go aside, withdraw, recoil, shrink back, Il.; δεῦρο λιάσθης hither has thou retired, id.; παρὰ κληῖδα λιάσθη, of a vision, slipped away by the key-hole, Od.; ἐλιάσθην πρός σε I came away to thee, Eur. 2. to sink, fall, πρηνὴς ἐλιάσθη, λιαζόμενος προτὶ γαίῃ Il. II. of things, λιάζετο κῦμα retired, drew back, id.; πτερὰ λίασθεν (for ἐλιάσθησαν) the dying bird's wings dropped, id. (deriv. uncertain)

λιαν.def: λίαν (λι-) very, exceedingly, Hom.; οὐδέ τι λ. οὕτω not so very much, Od.; with a Verb, very much, overmuch, exceedingly, Hom.; strengthd. καὶ λίην, as, aye truly, verily, id.; λίην πιστεύειν to believe implicitly, Hdt.; κόμπος λίαν εἰρημένος verily, truly, Aesch.; ἡ λίαν φιλότης his too great love, id.

λιαροσ.def: λιᾰρός, ή, όν (like χλιαρός) warm, Hom.; οὖρος λ. a warm soft wind, Od.; ὕπνος λ. balmy sleep, Il.

λιβαδιον.def: λῐβάδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λιβάς) a small stream, Strab.

λιβαζω.def: λιβάζω (λιβάς) =λείβω, to let fall in drops:— Mid. to run out in drops, trickle, Anth.

λιβανοσ.def: λῐ́βᾰνος, ὁ, I. the frankincense-tree, producing λιβανωτός, Hdt., etc. II. = λιβανωτός, in which sense it is fem., Eur., etc. (A foreign word.)

λιβανωτιζω.def: λῐβᾰνωτίζω, to fumigate with frankincense, Strab.

λιβανωτοσ.gloss: frankincense, the gum of the tree
λιβανωτοσ.def: λῐβᾰνωτός, οῦ, I. frankincense, the gum of the tree λίβανος, Hdt., Ar., etc. II. a censer, Lat. thuribulum, NTest.

λιβασ.def: λῐβάς, άδος, (λείβω) anything that drops or trickles, a spring, stream, Soph., Eur.: standing water, Babr.: —in pl. streams, pools, Aesch., Eur.

λιβερτινοσ.def: λιβερτῖνος, ὁ, the Lat. libertinus, a freedman, NTest.

λιβοσ.def: λίβος = λιβάς: λ. αἵματος a drop or fleck of blood, Aesch.: pl. λίβη tears, id.

λιβροσ.def: λιβρός, ή, όν (λείβω) dripping, wet, Anth.

λιβυη.gloss: Libya, the north part of Africa
λιβυη.def: Λῐβύη, ἡ, Libya, the north part of Africa west of Egypt, Od., Hdt.; in later writers also for the whole Continent

λιβυκοσ.def: Λιβυκός, ή, όν Libyan, Hdt., etc.

λιβυρνικοσ.def: Λιβυρνικός, ή, όν Liburnian; Λιβυρνικόν (sc. πλοῖον), a light vessel like a galley or felucca, such as was used by the Λιβυρνοί, Plut.; also Λιβυρνίς, ίδος, sc. ναῦς, id.

λιβυρνοι.def: Λιβυρνοί, οἱ, the Liburnians, a people on the Adriatic below Istria, Strab.

λιβυσ.def: Λῐ́βῠς, ῠος, ὁ, a Libyan, Hdt., etc.; and as adj. = Λιβυκός, Eur.; fem. Λίβυσσα, Pind.; also Λιβυστικός, ή, όν, Aesch.

λιβυφοινιξ.def: Λιβυφοῖνιξ a Liby-Phoenician, i. e. Carthaginian, Polyb.

λιγα.def: λίγα (adverb of λιγύς) in loud clear tone, Hom.

λιγαινω.def: λιγαίνω (λιγύς) (poetic verb, only in pres. and imperf.) I. to cry aloud, of heralds, Il.; of mourners, Aesch.; also, σύριγγι λ. to produce clear sounds on the pipe, to play on it, Anth.; c. acc. cogn., μέλος λ. Bion, Mosch. II. trans. to sing of, Anth.

λιγγω.def: λίγγω, only in epic aor1, λίγξε βιός the bow twanged, Il.

λιγδην.def: λίγδην just scraping, grazing, Lat. strictim, Od. (deriv. uncertain)

λιγνυσ.gloss: thick smoke mixed with flame, a murky flame
λιγνυσ.def: λιγνύς, ύος thick smoke mixed with flame, a murky flame, Aesch., Soph., Ar.; λιγνὺς πρόσεδρος in Soph. is the smoky flame hanging round Hercules.

λιγυασταδησ.def: Λιγυαστάδης, ου, ὁ, (λιγύς) a name borne by Mimnermus, Solon.

λιγυπτερυγοσ.def: λῐγυ-πτέρῠγος, ον (πτέρυξ) chirping with the wings, of the cicada, Anth.

λιγυροσ.def: λῐγῠρός, ή, όν I. clear, whistling, of winds, Il.; of a whip, id.; λιγυρὰ ἄχεα griefs which vent themselves in shrill wailings, Eur.:—also clear-voiced, sweet-toned, Hom., etc.:—neut. pl. as adv., λιγυρὰ ἀείδειν Theogn.; λιγυρῶς Theocr. II. pliant, flexible, of dogs' tails, Xen. (from λῐγύς)

λιγυσ.def: λιγύς I. clear, whistling, of winds, Hom.: of a clear, sweet sound, clear-toned, id.; of the nightingale, Aesch. II. adv. shrilly, Hom.; clearly, Il.:—neut. as adv., λιγὺ μέλπεσθαι Hes., Aesch.
Λῐ́γυς, υος a Ligurian, Hdt., Thuc., etc.:— adj. Λῐγυστικός, ή, όν Ligurian, Strab.

λιγυφθογγοσ.def: λῐγύ-φθογγος, ον (φθογγή) clear-voiced, of heralds, Hom.; of the nightingale, Ar.

λιγυφωνοσ.def: λῐγύ-φωνος, ον (φωνή) clear-voiced, loud-voiced, screaming, Il.; also of sweet sounds, Hes., Theocr.

λιθαζω.def: λῐθάζω, (λίθος) I. to fling stones, Strab. II. trans. to stone a man, NTest.

λιθαξ.def: λῐ́θαξ, ακος, (λίθος) I. stony, Od. II. as fem. Subst., = λίθος, a grave-stone, Anth.; of the pumice-stone, id.

λιθασ.def: λῐθάς, άδος, (= λίθος, Od.) collectively in sg., a shower of stones, Aesch.

λιθεια.def: λῐθεία, ἡ, (λίθος) I. a sort of fine stone or marble for building, Strab. II. a precious stone, id.

λιθεοσ.def: λῐ́θεος, η, ον (= λίθινος) of stone, Hom.

λιθηλογησ.def: λῐθη-λογής, ές (λέγω) built of stones, Anth.

λιθιαω.def: λῐθιάω, (only in pres.) to suffer from stone, Plat.

λιθιδιον.def: λῐθίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λίθος) a pebble, Plat.

λιθινοσ.def: λ̆ίθῐνος, η, ον (λίθος) of stone, Hdt., Plat., etc.; λ. θάνατος stony death, caused by seeing the Gorgon's head, Pind.; στῆναι λίθινος, of a statue, Hdt.

λιθοβλητοσ.def: λῐθό-βλητος, ον I. stone-throwing, pelting, Anth. II. set with stones, id.

λιθοβολεω.def: λῐθοβολέω, to pelt with stones, stone, NTest. (from λῐθοβόλος)

λιθοβολοσ.def: λῐθο-βόλος, ον (cf. λιθοβόλος) (βάλλω) proparox. λιθόβολος, ον, pass. struck with stones, stoned, Eur.
λῐθο-βόλος, ον (cf. λιθόβολος) (βάλλω) 1. throwing stones, pelting with stones: λιθοβόλοι, οἱ, stone-throwers, Thuc., etc. 2. λιθοβόλος, an engine for hurling stones, Polyb., etc.

λιθοδερκησ.def: λῐθο-δερκής, ές petrifying with a glance, Anth.

λιθοδομοσ.def: λῐθο-δόμος, ὁ, (δέμω) building with stones, a mason, Xen.

λιθοεργοσ.def: λῐθο-εργός, όν (⁎ἔργω) turning to stone, Anth.

λιθοκολλητοσ.def: λῐθο-κόλλητος, ον (κολλάω) I. set with precious stones, Theophr., Plut.:— λ. στόμιον a bit set with stones (to make it sharper), Soph. II. τὸ λ. inlaid work, mosaic, Strab.

λιθοκτονια.def: λῐθο-κτονία, ἡ, (κτείνω) death by stoning, Anth.

λιθολευστοσ.def: λῐθό-λευστος, ον (λεύω) stoned with stones: λ. Ἄρης death by stoning, Soph.

λιθολογημα.def: λῐθολόγημα, ατος, εος, a stone-building, Xen. (from λῐθολόγος)

λιθολογοσ.gloss: one who builds with stones picked out
λιθολογοσ.def: λῐθο-λόγος, ὁ, (λέγω) one who builds with stones picked out to fit their places, not cut square; then, generally = λιθοδόμος, a mason, Thuc., etc.

λιθοξοοσ.def: λῐθο-ξόος, ὁ, (ξέω) a stone or marble-mason, Anth., Luc.

λιθοποιοσ.def: λῐθο-ποιός, όν (ποιέω) turning to stone, Luc.

λιθορρινοσ.def: λῐθόρ-ρῑνος, ον with stony skin, Hhymn.

λιθοσ.def: λῐ́θος, ου, I. a stone, Hom., etc.: a precious stone, Hdt.: marble, id.:—proverb., λίθον ἕψειν to boil a stone, i. e. "to lose one's labour," Ar.;— of stupidity, λίθοι blocks, stones, id. 2. stone as a substance, opp. to wood, flesh, etc, Il., etc. II. also fem., Hom., Theocr.;—but the fem. was mostly used of some special stone, as the magnet, Eur., Plat.; of a touchstone, Plat.; ἡ διαφανὴς λ. a piece of crystal used for a burning glass, Ar. III. at Athens, λίθος (masc.) was a name for various blocks of stone used for rostra or tribunes, as, 1. the Bema of the Pnyx, Ar. 2. another in the ἀγορά used by the κήρυκες, Plut. 3. an altar in the ἀγορά, Dem. IV. a piece on a draughtboard, Theocr.

λιθοσπαδησ.def: λῐθο-σπᾰδὴς, ἁρμός, οῦ, ὁ, a chasm made by tearing out stones, Soph.

λιθοστρωτοσ.def: λῐθό-στρωτος, ον paved with stones, Soph.:— λιθόστρωτον, τό, a tesselated pavement, NTest.

λιθοτομια.gloss: a place where stone is cut, a quarry;
λιθοτομια.def: λῐθοτομία, ἡ, a place where stone is cut, a quarry; mostly in pl., quarries, Hdt., Thuc., etc. (from λῐθοτόμος)

λιθουργεω.def: λῐθουργέω, to turn into stone, petrify, Anth. (from λῐθουργός)

λιθουργοσ.def: λῐθ-ουργός, οῦ, ὁ, (⁎ἔργω) I. a worker in stone, stone-mason, Ar., Thuc. II. as adj., σιδήρια λιθουργά a stonemason's tools, Thuc.

λιθοφορεω.def: λῐθοφορέω, to carry stones, Thuc. (from λῐθοφόρος)

λιθοφοροσ.def: λῐθο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) carrying stones:—as Subst., = λιθοβόλος, Polyb.

λιθωδησ.def: λῐθώ-δης, ες (εἶδος) like stone, stony, Hdt., Xen.

λικμαιοσ.def: λικμαῖος, η, ον presiding over winnowing, Anth.

λικμαω.gloss: to part the grain from the chaff, to winnow
λικμαω.def: λικμάω, (λικμός) to part the grain from the chaff, to winnow, Il., Xen.:— metaph. to scatter like chaff, NTest.

λικμητηρ.def: λικμητήρ, ῆρος, (from λικμάω) a winnower of corn, Il.

λικνον.def: λίκνον, ου, τό, I. a winnowing-fan, i. e. a broad basket, in which the corn was placed after threshing, and then thrown against the wind:—it was sacred to Bacchus, cf. Virgil's mystica vannus Iacchi, Soph., Anth. II. the infant Bacchus was carried in it: hence a cradle, Hhymn., etc.

λικνοφοροσ.def: λικνο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) carrying the sacred λίκνον in procession, Dem.

λικριφισ.def: λικριφίς crosswise, sideways, Hom.; cf. λέχριος

λιλαιομαι.def: λιλαίομαι (Mid., only in pres. and imperf.) to long or desire earnestly, Il.; metaph. of a lance, λιλαιομένη χροὸς ἆσαι longing to taste flesh, id.; λιλαιομένη πόσιν εἶναι longing for him to be her husband, Od.: —also c. gen. to long for, λιλαιόμενοι πολέμοιο Il., etc.:—also, φόωσδε λιλαίεσθαι to struggle to the light of day, Od.

λιμαινω.def: λῑμαίνω, (λιμός) to suffer from hunger, Hdt.

λιμενιτησ.def: λῐ̄μενίτης, ου, ὁ, god of the harbour, Anth.: fem. λιμενῖτις, ιδος, id.

λιμενορμιτησ.def: λῐ̄μεν-ορμίτης, ου, ὁ, (ὁρμίζω) tarrying in the harbour, Anth.

λιμενοσκοποσ.def: λῐμενο-σκόπος, ον watching the harbour, Anth.

λιμην.def: λῐμήν, ένος, ὁ, I. a harbour, haven, creek, whereas ὅρμος is properly the inner part of the harbour, the landing-place, Hom., etc.; in pl., Od., Soph., etc.; —also c. gen. objecti, λιμένες θαλάσσης havens of refuge from the sea, Od. II. metaph. a haven, retreat, refuge, Theogn.; ἑταιρείας λ. a haven of friendship, Soph.; λ. τῶν ἐμῶν βουλευμάτων Eur.; c. gen. objecti, χείματος λ. a harbour of refuge from the storm, id. 2. a place of resort, receptacle, πλούτου λ. Aesch.; παντὸς οἰωνοῦ λ. Soph.; in O. T. 420, the sense seems to be—how will Cithaeron not be filled with thy cries (λιμὴν ἔσται τῆς σῆς βοῆς) ? how will it not reecho them?

λιμηροσ.def: λῑμηρός, ή, όν (λιμός) hungry, causing hunger, Theocr., Anth.
λῐμηρός, ή, όν (λιμήν) furnished with a good harbour, Thuc.

λιμναιοσ.def: λιμναῖος, η, ον (λίμνη) of or from the marsh or mere, ὄρνιθας χερσαίους τε καὶ λ. both land-fowl and water fowl, Hdt., Ar.

λιμνασ.def: λιμνάς, άδος, (poet. fem. of λιμναῖος, Theocr., Babr.)

λιμνη.def: λίμνη (λείβω) I. a pool of standing water left by the sea or a river, Il.: then, a marshy lake, mere, Lat. palus, id., Hdt., attic:—also, a large pool or basin (artificial), Hdt. 2. in Hom. and other Poets, the sea. II. Λίμναι, ῶν, αἱ, a quarter of Athens (once prob. marshy), near the Acropolis, in which stood the Lenaeum, Ar., Thuc., etc.

λιμνησιοσ.def: Λιμνήσιος, ὁ, laker, name of a frog, Batr.

λιμνητησ.def: λιμνήτης, ου, ὁ, I. living in marshes, Theocr. II. epith. of Artemis, dat. Λιμνᾶτι shortd. for Λιμνάτιδι, Anth.

λιμνουργοσ.def: λιμν-ουργός, οῦ, ὁ, (⁎ἔργω) one who works in λίμναι, a fisherman, Plut.

λιμνοχαρισ.def: λιμνόχαρις grace of the marsh, or -χαρής, love-marsh, name of a frog, Batr.

λιμνωδησ.def: λιμν-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) like a marsh, marshy: τὸ λιμνῶδες τοῦ Στρυμόνος the marshy ground at the mouth of the Strymon, Thuc.

λιμοθνησ.def: λῑμο-θνής, ῆτος, (θνήσκω) dying of hunger, Aesch.

λιμοκτονεω.def: λῑμο-κτονέω, (κτείνω) to kill by hunger, starve, Plat.

λιμοκτονια.def: λῑμοκτονία, ἡ, (from λῑμοκτονέω) a killing by hunger or by abstinence from food, Plat.

λιμοσ.def: λῑμός, οῦ, hunger, famine, Hom., etc.:— proverb., ἀπολεῖτε λιμῷ Μηλίῳ, referring to the siege of Melos, Ar.:—metaph., of the mind, Eur.

λιμοψωροσ.def: λῑμό-ψωρος, ὁ, (ψώρα) a cutaneous disease, scurvy, Polyb.

λιμωσσω.def: λῑμώσσω, (λιμός) to be famished, hungry, Strab., Anth.

λινεοσ.def: λῐ́νεος, η, ον (λίνον) of flax, flaxen, linen, Lat. lineus, Hdt., Plat., etc.

λινοδετοσ.def: λῐνό-δετος, ον (δέω) bound with flaxen cords, Eur.; λινόδετος τοῦ ποδός tied by the foot, Ar.

λινοθηρησ.def: λῐνο-θήρης, ου, ὁ, (θηράω) one who uses nets, Anth.

λινοθωρηξ.def: λῐνο-θώρηξ, ηκος, ὁ, wearing a linen cuirass, Il., Xen.

λινον.def: λῐ́νον, ου, τό, I. anything made of flax: 1. a cord, fishing-line, Il.: the thread spun from a distaff, Eur., etc.; and in pl., id.:—metaph. the thread of destiny spun by the Fates, Hom., Theocr.:—proverb., λίνον λίνῳ συνάπτειν, i. e. to join like with like, to deal with matters of like kind, Plat. 2. a fishing-net, Il.:— a hunting-net, Theocr. 3. linen, linen-cloth, Hom.: sail-cloth, Ar. 4. flax for spinning, id. II. the plant that produces flax, Lat. linum, Hdt., etc.; λίνου σπέρμα lint-seed, Thuc. III. on λίνον ἄειδεν, v. Λίνος II.

λινοπεπλοσ.def: λῐνό-πεπλος, ον with linen robe, Anth.

λινοπταομαι.gloss: to watch nets, see whether anything is caught
λινοπταομαι.def: λινοπτάομαι, (λινόπτης) Dep. to watch nets, see whether anything is caught, Ar.

λινοπτεροσ.def: λῐνό-πτερος, ον (πτερόν) sail-winged, of ships, Aesch.

λινοπτησ.gloss: one who watches nets to see whether anything is caught
λινοπτησ.def: λῐν-όπτης, ου, ὁ, (ὄψομαι, fut. of ὁράω) one who watches nets to see whether anything is caught, Arist.

λινοσ.def: Λῐ́νος, ου, I. Linos, a mythical minstrel, son of Apollo and Urania (Calliope), teacher of Orpheus, Theocr., etc. II. as appellat., the song or lay of Linos, sung by a boy to the cithara while the vintagers are at work, Λίνον ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδεν sang the lovely lay of Linos in accompaniment, Il.:—cf. αἴλινος which is a mournful song.

λινοστασια.gloss: a laying of nets: the nets laid
λινοστασια.def: λῐνο-στᾰσία, ἡ, a laying of nets: the nets laid, Anth.

λινουργοσ.def: λῐν-ουργός, οῦ, ὁ, (⁎ἔργω) a weaver, Strab.

λιπα.def: λίπα (λίπος) adv. unctuously, richly, ἀλεῖψαι or ἀλείψασθαι λίπ’ ἐλαίῳ to anoint or cause to be anointed richly with oil, Il.; so, χρῖσαι or χρίσασθαι λίπ’ ἐλαίῳ id.; only once without ἐλαίῳ, λοέσσατο καὶ λίπ’ ἄλειψεν Od. In all these places, the final vowel is uncertain; but we have λίπα ἀλείψασθαι, -εσθαι in Thuc., etc.

λιπαινω.def: λῐπαίνω, (λίπος) 1. to oil, anoint: Mid. to anoint oneself, Anth. 2. of rivers, to make fat, enrich, Eur.

λιπανδρεω.gloss: to be in want of men
λιπανδρεω.def: λῐπ-ανδρέω, (λείπομαι, ἀνήρ) to be in want of men, Strab.; λῐπ-ανδρία, want of men, id.

λιπαρα.def: Λῐπ̆άρα, ἡ, the largest of the Aeolian islands, Thuc., etc.:—adj. Λῐπᾰραῖος, η, ον of Lipara, αἱ Λ. νῆσοι the group of these islands, Polyb.

λιπαραμπυξ.def: λῐπᾰρ-άμπυξ, ῠκος, ὁ, ἡ, with bright tiara, Pind.

λιπαρεω.def: λῑπᾰρέω, I. to persist, persevere, hold out, Hdt.; so in part., διάγειν λιπαρέοντας to continue to hold out, id.; also, reversely, λιπαρέετε μένοντες persist in holding your ground, id.; so, c. dat., λ. τῇ πόσει to keep on drinking, id. II. of persistent entreaty, 1. absol. to persist in intreating, to be importunate, id., Aesch., etc. 2. c. acc. et inf. to importune one to do a thing, Aesch., Soph. 3. c. acc., λιπαρεῖν αὐτόν entreat earnestly for him, Dem. (from λῑπᾰρής)

λιπαρησ.def: λῑπᾰρής, ές I. persisting or persevering in a thing, earnest, indefatigable, Plat. 2. of things, Ar., Luc. II. earnest in begging or praying, importunate, λ. χείρ a hand instant in prayer, Soph.:— τὸ λιπαρές importunity, Luc.; πρὸς τὸ λ. λιπαρῶς, Soph. III. adv. -ρῶς, earnestly, importunately, Plat. (Deriv. uncertain: the first syll. seems to be from λι-, λίαν.)

λιπαρητεοσ.def: λῑπαρητέος, ον (verb. adj. of λιπαρέω) one must be importunate, Xen.

λιπαροκρηδεμνοσ.def: λῐπᾰρο-κρήδεμνος, ον with bright head-band, Il.

λιπαροπλοκαμοσ.def: λῐπᾰρο-πλόκᾰμος, ον with glossy locks, Il.

λιπαροσ.def: λῐπᾰρός, ή, όν (λίπος) I. oily, shiny with oil, acc. to the custom of oiling the skin in the palaestra, Od., Ar., etc. 2. oily, greasy, Ar. II. of the skin, shining, sleek, Lat. nitidus, λιπαροὶ πόδες bright, smooth feet, without a wrinkle, Il.; λιπαρώτεροι ἐγένοντο Hdt.; λ. στῆθος Ar., etc. III. of condition, rich, comfortable, easy, Lat. nitidus, lautus, Od., Pind.; so, λιπαρῶς γηράσκειν Od. IV. of things, bright, brilliant, costly, splendid, Hom. V. of soil, fat, rich, fruitful, Lat. pinguis, Hhymn., Theogn.; λιπαραὶ Ἀθῆναι, a favourite epith. with the Athenians, prob. with allusion to the Attic olive, Pind., Ar.

λιπαροχρουσ.def: λῐπᾰρό-χρους, ουν (χρόα) with shining skin, Theocr.

λιπαυγησ.def: λῐπ-αυγής, ές (αὐγή) deserted by light, blind, Anth.

λιπαω.def: λῐπάω, (λίπας, λίπος) to be fat and sleek, epic part. λιπόων Anth.

λιπερνησ.def: λῐπερνής, ές (Deriv. unknown.) desolate, forlorn, homeless, outcast, Archil.

λιπογαμοσ.def: λῐπό-γᾰμος, ον having abandoned her marriage ties, of Helen, Eur.

λιπογυιοσ.def: λῐπό-γυιος, ον (γυῖον) wanting a limb, maimed, Anth.

λιπομαρτυριον.def: λιπομαρτύριον (λείπω, μαρτύριον) λῐπο-μαρτῠρίου δίκη, an action against a witness for non-appearance, Dem.

λιποναυτησ.def: λῐπο-ναύτης, ου, ὁ, leaving the sailors, Theocr.

λιποπατρισ.def: λῐπό-πατρις, ιδος causing to forget one's country, of the lotos, Anth.

λιποπατωρ.def: λῐπο-πᾰ́τωρ, ορος, (πατήρ) deserter of one's father, Eur.

λιποπνουσ.def: λῐπό-πνους, ουν (πνοή) left by breath, breathless, dead, Anth.

λιποσ.def: λῐ́πος, εος, fat, βεβρῶτες αἵματος λίπος gorged with fat and blood, Soph.

λιποστεφανοσ.def: λῐπο-στέφᾰνος, ον falling from the wreath, Anth.

λιποστρατια.gloss: desertion of the army, refusal to serve
λιποστρατια.def: λῐπο-στρᾰτία, ἡ, desertion of the army, refusal to serve, Hdt., Thuc.

λιποταξια.def: λῐπο-ταξία, ἡ, a leaving one's post, desertion, Dem.

λιποταξιον.def: λῐπο-ταξίου, γραφή, ἡ, λῐπο-ταξίου γραφή, ἡ, an indictment for desertion, Plat., Dem.

λιποτριχησ.def: λῐπο-τρῐχής, ές (θρίξ) having lost one's hair, Anth.

λιποψυχεω.def: λῐπο-ψῡχέω, (ψυχή) I. to leave life, swoon, Thuc., Xen. II. to lack spirit, fail in courage, Hdt.

λιπτομαι.def: λίπτομαι, Dep., with perf. pass. λέλιμμαι, to be eager, Aesch.:—c. gen. to be eager for, long for, id.

λισ.def: λίς (epic for λέων) (only in nom. and acc.) a lion, Il., Hes., Theocr.

λίς, ίδος (epic form for λισσή) I. smooth, Od. II. as masc. Subst., only in dat. λιτί and acc. λῖτα, smooth cloth, linen cloth: others take λῖτα to be acc. pl. neut. linen cloths:—in Anth., we have λίτα [ῐ] πολυδαίδαλα, embroidered stuffs.

λισποσ.def: λίσπος, η, ον (λίς) I. smooth, polished, Ar. II. as Subst. λίσπαι, ῶν, αἱ, dice cut in two by friends (ξένοι), each of whom kept half as tallies (σύμβολα), Plat.

λισσασ.def: λισσάς, άδος, (pecul. fem. of λισσός) I. smooth, bare, Eur., Theocr. II. as Subst. a bare, smooth cliff, Plut.
