λισσομαι.def: λίσσομαι 1. to beg, pray, entreat, beseech, either absol. or c. acc. pers., Hom.; that by which one prays, in gen., λ. τινα γούνων Il.; λ. Ζηνός Od.:—an inf. is often added, οὐδέ ς’ ἔγωγε λίσσομαι μένειν I do not pray thee to remain, Il. 2. c. acc. rei, to beg or pray for, οἷ αὐτῶι θάνατον λιτέσθαι id.: c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, ταῦτα μὲν οὐχ ὑμέας ἔτι λίσσομαι this I beg of you no more, Od.

λισσοσ.def: λισσός, ή, όν (λίς) smooth, λισσὴ αἰπεῖά τε εἰς ἅλα πέτρη a smooth rock running sheer into the sea, Od.; λισσὴ δ’ ἀναδέδρομε πέτρη id.

λιστοσ.def: λιστός, ή, όν (λίσσομαι) to be moved by prayer, ap. Plat.

λιστρευω.def: λιστρεύω, to dig round a plant, Od. (from λίστρον)

λιστρον.def: λίστρον, ου, τό, a tool for levelling or smoothing, a spade, a kind of shovel, Od., Mosch. (deriv. uncertain)

λιτανευω.def: λῐτᾰνεύω, (λίτομαι) to pray, entreat, esp. for protection, either absol. or c. acc. pers., Hom.; that by which one prays in gen., γούνων λιτανεύειν Od.; also, γούνων ἁψάμενοι λιτανεύσομεν (epic for -ωμεν), Il.; c. inf., id.

λιτανοσ.def: λῐτᾰνός, ή, όν (λιτή) praying, suppliant, μέλη Aesch.: —as Subst., λιτανά, τά, λιταί, ἀμφὶ λιτᾰνὰ ἔχεσθαι to be engaged in prayer, id.

λιτη.def: λῐτή, ἡ, (λίτομαι) I. a prayer, entreaty, mostly in pl., Od., Hdt., Trag. II. Λιταί, Prayers of sorrow and repentance, personified in Il. 9. 502 sq.

λιτοβιοσ.def: λῑτό-βιος, ον (λῑτός) living plainly or sparingly, Strab.

λιτοσ.def: λῐτός, ή, όν (λίτομαι) suppliant, supplicatory, Pind.
λῑτός, ή, όν (v. λίς) 1. smooth, plain: of style, simple, unadorned, Arist.: of persons, simple, frugal, Polyb.: adv. λιτῶς, Anth. 2. paltry, petty, id.

λιτρα.def: λίτρα, ἡ, a silver coin of Sicily, Lat. libra:—as a weight, 12 ounces, a pound, Anth.:—metaph., λίτρᾰν ἐτῶν ζήσας having lived a pound of years, i. e. 72 (for a pound of gold was coined into 72 pieces), id.

λιτραιοσ.def: λῑτραῖος, η, ον weighing or worth a λίτρα, Anth.

λιτρον.def: λίτρον, ου, τό, (older form for νίτρον, Hdt., Plat.)

λιτυερσησ.def: Λιτυέρσης Lityerses, a son of Midas: a reaper's song named after him, Theocr.

λιτυον.def: λίτυον, ου, τό, the Roman lituus, Plut.

λιχανοσ.def: λιχᾰνός, όν (λείχω) the fore-finger, from its use in licking up, Luc.

λιχμαζω.def: λιχμάζω, (λείχω) I. = λιχμάω, Hes. II. trans. to lick, ionic 3rd sg. imperf. λιχμάζεσκε Mosch.

λιχμαω.def: λιχμάω (λείχω) to lick with the tongue, of snakes, Eur.:—Mid., ἐλιχμῶντο περὶ τὴν κεφαλήν played like serpents round the head, Ar.

λιχνεια.def: λιχνεία, ἡ, daintiness, greediness, Xen., Plat. (from λιχνεύω)

λιχνευω.def: λιχνεύω, (λίχνος) I. to lick, Luc. II. to lick up:— metaph. to desire greedily, covet, δόξαν Plut.

λιχνοβοροσ.def: λιχνο-βόρος, ον (βιβρώσκω) nice in eating, dainty, Anth.

λιχνοσ.def: λίχνος, η, ον (λείχω) 1. dainty, lickerish, greedy, Xen., Plat. 2. metaph. curious, Eur.

λιψ.def: λίψ (from λείβω, because it brought wet) the SW. wind, Lat. Africus, Hdt., Theocr.
λίψ (λείβω) (only in gen. and acc. λιβάς or λίβος being used as nom.) a stream, Aesch.: a draught, id.

λιψουρια.gloss: desire of making water, natural needs
λιψουρια.def: λιψ-ουρία, ἡ, (οὖρον) desire of making water, natural needs, Aesch.

λοβοσ.def: λοβός, οῦ, (λέπω) 1. the lobe of the ear, Il. 2. the lobe of the liver, Aesch., Eur.: generally, the liver, Aesch.

λογαδην.def: λογάδην (λογάς) by picking out, of stones for building, Thuc.; of soldiers, Plut.

λογαριον.def: λογᾱ́ριον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λόγος) λ. δύστηνα wretched petty speeches, Dem.

λογασ.def: λογάς, άδος, (λέγω) 1. gathered, picked, chosen, of picked men, Hdt., Eur., etc. 2. λ. λίθοι unhewn stones, taken just as they were picked, cf. λογάδην.

λογειον.def: λογεῖον, ου, τό, (λόγος) properly a speaking-place: in the attic theatre, the part of the stage occupied by the speakers, Lat. pulpitum, Plut., etc.

λογια.def: λογία, ἡ, (λέγω) a collection for the poor, NTest.

λογιδιον.def: λογίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λόγος) a little fable or story, Ar.

λογιζομαι.def: λογίζομαι (λόγος) I. to count, reckon, calculate, compute, Hdt.; λ. ἀπὸ χειρός to calculate off hand, Ar.:—c. acc. rei, λ. τοὺς τόκους to calculate the interest, id.; τρεῖς μνᾶς ἀναλώσας λογίσασθαι δώδεκα to spend 3 minae and set down 12, id. 2. c. acc. et inf. to reckon or calculate that, Hdt., Dem. 3. λ. τί τινι to set down to one's account, charge to one, Lat. imputare, Dem., NTest. 4. λογ. ἀπό.. to deduct from.., Dem. II. without reference to numbers, to take into account, calculate, consider, Hdt., attic; λ. περί τινος to form calculations about.., Hdt., Xen. 2. c. acc. et inf. to count, deem, consider that.., Hdt., attic; with the inf. omitted, to reckon or account so and so, τὸν καθ’ ἡμέραν βίον λογίζου σόν Eur.; μίαν ἄμφω τὰς ἡμέρας λ. to count both days as one, Xen. 3. c. inf. fut. to count or reckon upon doing, to calculate or expect that.., Hdt., Xen.;—c. acc. only, to count upon, Soph. 4. to conclude by reasoning, infer that a thing is, Plat., Xen. III. the aor1 ἐλογίσθην and sometimes perf. λελόγισμαι are used in pass. sense, to be counted or calculated, Xen.

λογιμοσ.def: λόγιμος, η, ον (λόγος) worth mention, notable, remarkable, famous, Hdt.

λογιον.def: λόγιον, ου, τό, (λόγος) an announcement, oracle, Hdt.; in pl. oracles, id., Eur., etc.

λογιοσ.def: λόγιος, η, ον (λόγος) I. versed in tales or stories (λόγος IV): as Subst. a chronicler, annalist, Hdt. 2. generally learned, erudite, Arist., etc. II. skilled in words, eloquent, Eur., Plut.

λογισμοσ.def: λογισμός, οῦ, ὁ, (λογίζομαι) I. a counting, reckoning, calculation, computation, Thuc., Plat.:—in pl. arithmetic, Xen., Plat. 2. an account, bill, Dem. II. without reference to number, calculation, consideration, reasoning, Thuc., Dem. 2. an argument, conclusion, Xen. III. reasoning power, reason, id.

λογιστεοσ.def: λογιστέος, ον (verb. adj. of λογίζομαι,) one must calculate or subtract, Dem.

λογιστηριον.def: λογιστήριον, ου, τό, the place at Athens where the λογισταί met, Oratt. (from λογιστής)

λογιστησ.def: λογιστής, οῦ, (λογίζομαι) I. a calculator, teacher of arithmetic, Plat. 2. a calculator, reasoner, Ar., Dem. II. in pl. auditors, at Athens, ten members of the βουλή, to whom magistrates going out of office submitted their accounts, Dem., etc.

λογιστικοσ.def: λογιστικός, ή, όν (from λογιστής) I. skilled or practised in calculating, Xen., Plat.:— ἡ λογιστική (sc. τέχνη), arithmetic, Plat. II. endued with reason, rational, Arist.:— τὸ λ. the reasoning faculty, Plat. 2. using one's reason, reasonable, Xen.

λογογραφια.def: λογογρᾰφία, ἡ, a writing of speeches, and, generally, of prose, Plat.

λογογραφικοσ.def: λογογραφικός of or for writing speeches or prose, Plat. (from λογογρᾰ́φος)

λογογραφοσ.def: λογο-γρᾰ́φος, ὁ, (γράφω) I. a prose-writer:—the early Greek chroniclers are so called by Thuc. II. like λογοποιός II, a speech-writer, one who lived by writing speeches for others to deliver, Plat., etc.

λογολεσχησ.def: λογο-λέσχης, ου, ὁ, (λέσχη) a prater, Anth.

λογομαχεω.def: λογομᾰχέω, to war about words, NTest.

λογομαχια.def: λογομαχία a war about words, NTest. (from λογομάχος)

λογοποιεω.gloss: to invent stories, to write, compose
λογοποιεω.def: λογοποιέω, I. to invent stories, to write, compose, Plat. 2. to fabricate tales, of newsmongers, Thuc., Dem., etc. II. to write speeches (v. λογοποιός II), Plat.

λογοποιια.def: λογοποιία, ἡ, (from λογοποιέω) tale-telling, news-mongering, Theophr.

λογοποιικοσ.def: λογοποιικός, ή, όν of or like a λογοποιός: ἡ -κὴ τέχνη, λογογραφική, Plat.

λογοποιοσ.def: λογο-ποιός, οῦ, ὁ, (ποιέω) I. a prose-writer, esp. an historian, chronicler, Plat., etc. 2. a writer of fables, Hdt., Plut. II. = λογογράφος II, Plat. 2. a tale-teller, newsmonger, Dem.

λογοσ.def: λόγος, ὁ, (λέγω) (A) the word or that by which the inward thought is expressed, Lat. oratio; and, (B) the inward thought itself, Lat. ratio. A. Lat. vox, oratio, that which is said or spoken: I. a word, pl. words, i. e. language, talk, Hom., etc.; λόγου ἕνεκα, Lat. dicis causa, merely for talking's sake, Plat.; λόγῳ in word, in pretence, opp. to ἔργῳ (in deed, in reality), Hdt., attic II. a word, saying, statement, Thuc.: an oracle, Pind., Plat.:— a saying, maxim, proverb, Pind., Aesch. 2. an assertion, promise, Soph. 3. a resolution, κοινῷ λ. by common consent, Hdt. 4. a condition, ἐπὶ λόγῳ τοιῷδε id. 5. a command, Aesch. III. speech, discourse, conversation, εἰς λόγους ἐλθεῖν, συνελθεῖν, ἀφικέσθαι τινί Hdt., attic; λόγου μεῖζον, κρεῖσσον beyond expression, Hdt., Thuc.; λόγου ἄξιον worth mention, Hdt. 2. right of speech, power to speak, λόγον αἰτεῖσθαι Thuc.; διδόναι Xen. 3. talk about one, report, repute, Lat. fama, λόγος, Hdt., attic; λόγος ἐστί, λόγος ἔχει, κατέχει, φέρεται, c. acc. et inf., so the story goes, Lat. fama fert, Hdt., attic 4. speech, language, Plat. IV. a saying, tale, story, opp. on the one hand to mere fable (μῦθος), on the other, to regular history (ἱστορία), Hdt., Thuc., etc.: then, a fictitious story, fable, like those of Aesop, Hdt., Plat. 2. a narrative, and in pl. histories, history, Hdt.: in sg. one part of such a work, id. V. generally, prose-writing, prose, Xen., etc. VI. a speech, oration, Oratt. VII. like ῥῆμα, the thing spoken of, the subject or matter of the λόγος, Hdt., attic VIII. that which is stated, a proposition, position, principle, Plat.: also = ὁρισμός, a definition, id. B. Lat. ratio, thought, reason, οὐκ ἔχει λόγον admits not of reason, Soph.; ὀρθὸς λ. Plat.; ὡς ἔχει λόγον, ὡς ἔοικεν, Dem.:— κατὰ λόγον agreeably to reason, Plat.; μετὰ λόγου id. 2. an opinion, expectation, Hdt. 3. a reason, ground, plea, Soph., etc.; ἐκ τίνος λόγου; on what ground? Aesch.; ἐξ οὐδενὸς λ. Soph., etc. 4. ὁ λόγος αἱρέει, c. acc. et inf., it stands to reason that.., Lat. ratio evincit, Hdt. II. account, consideration, esteem, regard, λόγον βροτῶν οὐκ ἔσχεν οὐδένα Aesch.; Μαρδονίου λόγος οὐδεὶς γίγνεται Hdt.; λόγου οὐδενὸς γενέσθαι to be of no account, id.; λόγου ποιεῖσθαί τινα or τι, to make account of a person or thing, id.;—so, ἐν οὐδενὶ λόγῳ ποιεῖσθαι id.;— ἐν ἀνδρὸς λόγῳ εἶναι to be reckoned as a man, id. 2. an account, λόγον διδόναι τινός to give an account of a thing, id., attic; so, λόγον παρέχειν Plat.; λ. λαμβάνειν παρά τινος Dem.; λ. ἀπαιτεῖν id.; ὑπέχειν Plat., Dem., etc.; ἐγγράφειν Dem., etc.; ἀποφέρειν Aeschin.; cf. λογιστής. III. due relation, proportion, analogy, κατὰ λόγον τινός or τινί Hdt., attic C. Ὁ ΛΟΓ́ΟΣ, the Logos or Word, comprising both senses of Thought and Word, NTest.

λογχευω.def: λογχεύω, to pierce with a spear, Anth. (from λόγχη)

λογχη.def: λόγχη, ἡ, I. a spear-head, javelin-head, Lat. spiculum, Hdt., attic; in pl. of a single spear, the point with its barbs, τὸ ξυστὸν τῇσι λόγχῃσι ὁμοίως the shaft alike with the spear-head, Hdt. II. a lance, spear, javelin, Lat. lancea, Pind., Soph., etc. III. a troop of spearmen, "a plump of spears, " Soph., Eur.

λογχηρησ.def: λογχ-ήρης, ες (⁎ἄρω) armed with a spear, Eur.

λογχιμοσ.def: λόγχῐμος, ον (λόγχη) of a spear, κλόνοι λ. the clash of spears, Aesch.

λογχοομαι.gloss: to be furnished with a point
λογχοομαι.def: λογχόομαι, Pass. to be furnished with a point, Arist.

λογχοφοροσ.def: λογχο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) spear-bearing, Eur.: as Subst. a spear-man, pike-man, Ar., Xen., etc.

λογχωτοσ.def: λογχωτός, ή, όν lance-headed, Eur., Anth.

λοιβειον.def: λοιβεῖον, ου, τό, a cup for pouring libations, Plut. (from λοιβή)

λοιβη.def: λοιβή, ἡ, (λείβω) a drink-offering, Lat. libatio, Hom.; opt. in pl., Pind., Soph.

λοιγιοσ.def: λοίγιος, ον (λοιγός) pestilent, deadly, fatal, Il.

λοιγοσ.def: λοιγός, οῦ, ruin, havoc, of death by plague, Il.; by war, id.; of the destruction of the ships, id.

λοιδορεω.def: λοιδορέω (λοίδορος) I. to abuse, revile, Hdt., attic; to rebuke, Xen.:—Mid. to rail at one another, Ar. II. λοιδοροῦμαι is also used as Dep., c. dat., to rail at, id., Xen.:—c. acc. cogn., πάντα τὰ αἰσχρὰ λοιδορέονται they use all kind of foul reproaches, Hdt.

λοιδορημα.def: λοιδόρημα, ατος, εος, railing, abuse, an affront, Arist.

λοιδορια.def: λοιδορία, ἡ, (λοιδορέω) railing, abuse, Thuc., Plat.

λοιδοροσ.def: λοίδορος, ον railing, abusive, Eur.:—adv. -ρως, Strab. (deriv. uncertain)

λοιμοσ.def: λοιμός, οῦ, 1. a plague, pestilence, Il., Hdt., attic; of the plague at Athens, Thuc. 2. of persons, a plague, pest, Dem. (Prob. akin to λύμη, Lat. lues.)

λοιμωδησ.def: λοιμ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) like plague, pestilential, ἡ λ. νόσος the plague, Thuc.

λοιμωσσω.def: λοιμώσσω, to have the plague, Luc.

λοιποσ.def: λοιπός, ή, όν (λείπω) 1. remaining, the rest, Lat. reliquus, Hdt., etc.; in attic the Art. may either be in the same case as the Noun or have the Noun in gen. dependent on it, τὴν λοιπὴν ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι Xen.; αἱ λοιπαὶ τῶν νεῶν Thuc.; also, τὸ λοιπὸν τῆς ἡμέρας Xen. 2. λοιπόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it remains to shew, etc., Plat., Xen.; with Art., τὸ λ. ἐστι σκέψασθαι what remains is to consider, Plat.:— ὃ δὲ λοιπόν, quod superest, Aesch., etc. 3. often of Time, ὁ λ. χρόνος the future, Pind., attic; πρὸς τὸν λοιπὸν τοῦ χρόνου Dem.; τὸν λ. χρόνον for the future, Soph.; τοῦ λ. χρόνου id.;—so in neut., τὸ λοιπόν henceforward, hereafter, Trag.; so, τὰ λοιπά id. 4. τὸ λοιπόν and τὰ λοιπά the rest, Aesch.; also λοιπόν as adv., further, besides, Plat.

λοισθηιοσ.def: λοισθήιος, ον (epic for λοίσθιος) λοισθήιον ἄεθλον the prize for the last in the race, Il.

λοισθιοσ.def: λοίσθιος, ον = λοῖσθος, Pind., Trag.:—neut. λοίσθιον, as adv. last, Soph., Eur.

λοισθοσ.def: λοῖσθος, ον (= λοῖπος,) left behind, last, Il., Eur.;Sup. λοισθότατος last of all, Hes.

λοκκη.def: λόκκη, ἡ, a cloak, Anth. (deriv. uncertain)

λοκροι.def: Λοκροί, οἱ, the Locrians, of which there were three tribes, the Opuntian, opposite Euboea, Il.; the Epicnemidian, on Mount Cnemis on the Maliac Gulf, Thuc.; and the Ozolian, on the Corinthian Gulf, id.:— the Epizephyrian or Zephyrian were a colony of the last on Mount Zephyrium in lower Italy, Pind., Thuc.

λοκροσ.def: Λοκρός, ή, όν Locrian, fem. Λοκρίς, ίδος, Pind.; ἡ Λοκρίς (sc. γῆ), Ar.

λοξιασ.def: Λοξίας epith. of Apollo, Hdt., Trag.;—either from λοξός, the ambiguous, or from λέγω, λόγος, the speaker.

λοξοβατησ.def: λοξο-βᾰ́της, ου, ὁ, (βῆμα) going side-ways, Batr.

λοξοσ.def: λοξός, ή, όν 1. slanting, crosswise, aslant, Lat. obliquus, Eur.; λοξὰ βαίνειν, of a crab, Babr.; ὁ λοξὸς κύκλος the ecliptic, Arist. 2. of suspicious looks, λοξὸν ὁρᾶν to look askance, Lat. limis oculis, Solon.; λοξὰ βλ. Theocr.; αὐχένα λοξὸν ἔχειν to turn the neck aside, i. e. withdraw his favour, Tyrtae.; also = Horace's stare capite obstipo, Theogn. 3. of language, indirect, ambiguous, of oracles, Luc.

λοξοτησ.def: λοξότης, ητος, (from λοξός) slanting direction, obliquity, Strab.

λοξωσισ.def: λόξωσις, ιος obliquity, of the ecliptic, Anth., Strab.

λοπαδιον.def: λοπᾰ́διον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λοπάς,) a platter, Ar.

λοπασ.def: λοπάς, άδος, a flat dish, Ar.

λοποσ.def: λοπός, οῦ, (λέπω) the shell, husk, peel, λοπὸς κρομύοιο the peel of an onion, Od.

λουτροδαικτοσ.def: λουτρο-δάϊκτος, ον (δαΐζω) slain in the bath, Aesch.

λουτρον.def: λουτρόν, οῦ, (λούω) I. a bath, bathing place, Hom.; mostly in pl., θερμὰ λοετρά hot baths, Il.; attic θερμὰ λουτρά Aesch., etc.; also called λουτρὰ Ἡράκλεια Ar.; ὑδάτων λουτρά water for bathing or washing, Soph.; λοῦσαι τινα λουτρόν to give one a bath, id. II. in Poets, = σπονδαί or χοαί libations to the dead, id., Eur.

λουτροφοροσ.def: λουτρο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) 1. bringing water for bathing or washing, esp. from the fountain Callirrhoe on the wedding-day: hence, λ. χλιδή the marriage-ceremony, Eur. 2. as Subst., λουτροφόρος, the black urn placed on the tomb of unmarried persons, Dem., Anth.

λουτροχοεω.gloss: to pour water into the bath
λουτροχοεω.def: λουτροχοέω, to pour water into the bath, Anth.

λουτροχοοσ.gloss: pouring water into the bath, the slave who did this
λουτροχοοσ.def: λουτρο-χόος, ον (χέω) pouring water into the bath, the slave who did this, Od., Xen.; λ. τρίπους a three-legged kettle, in which water was warmed for bathing, Hom.

λουτρων.def: λουτρών, ῶνος, (λουτρόν) a bathing-room, bath-house, Aesch., Xen.

λουω.def: λούω I. to wash another, properly, to wash his body (νίζω being used of the hands and feet, πλύνω of clothes), Hom.; λούσατε ἐν ποταμῶι bathe him, i. e. let him bathe, Od.:—also, λό’ ἐκ τρίποδος washed me [with water] from a caldron, id. II. Mid. and Pass. to bathe, c. gen., λελουμένος Ὠκεανοῖο (of a star just risen), fresh from Ocean's bath, Il.;so, λούεσθαι ποταμοῖο to bathe [in water] of the river, id.; so, ἀπὸ κρήνης λούμενος Hdt.:—absol., λούσαντο Od., etc.; λελουμένος fresh-bathed, after bathing, Hdt.; ἦλθε λουσόμενος (Hor., ire lavatum), Ar. 2. in strict pass. sense, λοῦσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ Διός, i. e. to be washed by the rain from heaven, Hdt. 3. in strict mid. sense, λοέσσασθαι χρόα to wash one's body, Hes.

λοφαω.def: λοφάω 1. to have a crest (λόφος), of larks, Babr. 2. to be ill of a crest (i. e. to have more crest than enought), Ar.

λοφειον.def: λοφεῖον, ου, τό, (λόφος) a crest-case, Ar.: any case, id.

λοφηφοροσ.def: λοφη-φόρος, ον (φέρω) crested, of a lark, Babr.

λοφια.def: λοφιά, ιονιξ -ιή, ἡ, (λόφος) 1. the mane on the neck and back of certain animals, the mane of horses, the bristly back of boars and hyaenas, Od., Hdt. 2. the back-fin of fishes, Anth.

λοφιητησ.def: λοφιήτης, ου, ὁ, (from λοφιά) a dweller on the hills, of Pan, Anth.

λοφνισ.def: λοφνίς, ίδος (λέπω) a torch of vine bark, Anth.

λοφοποιοσ.def: λοφο-ποιός, οῦ, ὁ, (ποιέω) a crest-maker, Ar.

λοφοσ.def: λόφος, ου, I. properly the back of the neck of draught-cattle, because the yoke rubs it (λέπει); of a horse, the mane, Il.; of a man, the nape of the neck, id.; ὑπὸ ζυγῷ λόφον ἔχειν to have the neck under the yoke, i. e. to obey patiently, Soph. II. the crest of a hill, a ridge, Od., Hdt., etc. III. the crest of a helmet, Lat. crista, Hom., etc. 2. the crest on the head of birds, Lat. crista, as of the lark, Simon.; the cock's comb, Ar. 3. of men, the tuft of hair upon the crown, λόφους κείρεσθαι to shave so as to leave tufts, Hdt.

λοφωσισ.def: λόφωσις, ιος (λοφόομαι) a being crested, ἡ λ. ἡ τῶν ὀρνέων their crests, Ar.

λοχαγετησ.def: λοχᾱγέτης, ου, ὁ, (doric and attic for λοχηγέτης) (= λοχαγός, Aesch., Eur.)

λοχαγεω.def: λοχᾱγέω, to lead a λόχος or company (commonly of 100 men), Xen.; c. gen., λόχου λοχηγεῖν Hdt. (doric and attic for λοχηγέω,)

λοχαγια.def: λοχᾱγία, ἡ, the rank or office of λοχαγός, Xen. (doric and attic for λοχηγία,)

λοχαγοσ.gloss: the leader of an armed band
λοχαγοσ.def: λοχ-ᾱγός, οῦ, (λόχος, ἡγέομαι ἄγω) (doric and attic for λοχηγός,) I. the leader of an armed band, Soph. II. esp. the captain of a company (100 men), Xen.: —but, in the Spartan army, the commander of a λόχος, id.; in the Persian, of 24 men, id.

λοχαιοσ.def: λοχαῖος, η, ον (= λόχιος,) clandestine, Anth.

λοχαω.gloss: to lie in wait for, to watch, waylay, entrap
λοχαω.def: λοχάω, (λόχος) 1. to lie in wait for, to watch, waylay, entrap, Od., Hdt. 2. absol. to lie in wait or ambush, Il., Hdt.; in aor1 part. with another Verb, λοχήσας πολλοὺς διέφθειρεν Thuc.; Mid., λοχησάμενος Od. 3. c. acc. loci, to occupy with an ambuscade, ἐλόχησαν τὴν ὁδόν Hdt.

λοχεια.def: λοχεία, ἡ, (λοχεύω) I. childbirth, childbed, Eur., Plat. II. = λόχευμα I, Anth.

λοχειοσ.def: λοχεῖος, η, ον (= λόχιος, λοχεῖα (sub. χωρία）) the place of childbirth, Eur.

λοχευμα.gloss: that which is born, a child
λοχευμα.def: λόχευμα, ατος, εος, (λοχεύω) I. that which is born, a child, Eur. II. in pl., childbirth, id.: metaph., κάλυκος ἐν λοχεύμασιν in the bursting of the bud, Aesch.

λοχευω.def: λοχεύω, (λόχος II) I. to bring forth, bear, Hhymn., Anth. 2. of the midwife, to bring to the birth. attend in childbirth, deliver, τινά Eur.:—Pass. to be delivered, bear children, id.; λοχευθεῖσα πυρί, of Semele, id. II. Mid., just like Act., of the mother, Eur.; of the birthplace, Anth. III. Pass., of the child, to be brought forth, born, Soph.; Προμᾱθεῖ λοχευθεῖσα brought to birth by Prometheus, Eur.: —metaph., generally, to lie embedded, ἐν τεύτλοισι Ar.

λοχιζω.def: λοχίζω, (= λοχάω,) I. to lie in wait for, τινά: Pass., λοχισθέντες διεφθάρησαν they were cut to pieces by falling into an ambuscade, Thuc. 2. to place in ambush, id. II. to distribute men in companies (λόχοι), to put them in order of battle, Hdt., Plut.

λοχιοσ.def: λόχιος, η, ον I. of or belonging to childbirth, λ. νοσήματα childbed, Eur.; ὠδίνων λοχίαις ἀνάγκαις id. II. Λοχία, epith. of Artemis Εἰλείθυια, id. III. λόχια, ων, τά, childbirth, Anth.

λοχισμοσ.def: λοχισμός, οῦ, ὁ, (λοχίζω) a placing in ambush, Plut.

λοχιτησ.gloss: one of the same company, a fellow-soldier, comrade
λοχιτησ.def: λοχῑ́της, ου, ὁ, (λόχος) one of the same company, a fellow-soldier, comrade, Aesch., Xen.

λοχμαιοσ.def: λοχμαῖος, η, ον of the coppice, Μοῦσα λ., of the nightingale, Ar.

λοχμη.def: λόχμη, ἡ, (λόχος) a thicket, coppice, copse, Od., Pind.

λοχμωδησ.def: λοχμ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) overgrown with bushes, Thuc.

λοχονδε.def: λόχονδε to ambush, for an ambuscade, Hom.

λοχοσ.def: λόχος, ὁ, (λέγω) I. an ambush, i. e. 1. a place of ambush, place for lying in wait, Hom., Eur. 2. the act of lying in wait, λόχον εἷσαι to place an ambuscade, Hom.; λέγεσθαι ἐς λόχον to lie in ambush, Il.:—c. gen. objecti, λόχος θείοιο γέροντος the way to watch him, Od. 3. the men that form the ambush, Il., Eur. 4. any armed band, a body of troops, Od., Trag.:— a body of soldiers, a company, regiment, Xen.:—among the Spartans, a λόχος was the fourth or fifth part of a μόρα Hdt.:— ὁ ἱερὸς λ. the sacred company at Thebes, Plut. 5. any body of people, a union for civil purposes, Xen., etc.:—used to transl. the Rom. centuria, Plut., etc. II. a lying-in, childbirth, parturition, Aesch.

λυαιοσ.def: Λυαῖος, ὁ, (λύω) Deliverer, of Bacchus, Anacreont.

λυγαιοσ.def: λῡγαῖος, η, ον (λύγη) shadowy, murky, gloomy, Eur.

λυγδινοσ.def: λύγδῐνος, η, ον 1. of white marble, Babr., Anth. 2. marble-white, Anth. (from λύγδος)

λυγιζω.def: λῠγίζω, (λύγος) I. to bend or twist as one does a withe, πλευρὰν λ. of a dancer, Ar.; λ. ἀλλήλους, of wrestlers, Luc. 2. to throw, master, Theocr. II. Pass. to bend or twist oneself like a withe, to bend aside or writhe, so as to avoid a blow, Plat., Luc.:—metaph., in perf. part. λελυγισμένος, broken, effeminate, Anth. 2. to turn, play, as a joint in the socket, Soph. 3. metaph. to be thrown or mastered, Theocr.

λυγισμοσ.def: λῠγισμός, οῦ, (from λῠγίζω) a bending, twisting, of wrestlers, Luc.: metaph., of the windings and twistings of a sophist, Ar.

λυγκειοσ.def: λύγκειος, η, ον (λύγξ, ὁ) lynx-like, Anth.

λυγξ.gloss: a spasmodic affection of the throat, hiccough, hiccup
λυγξ.def: λύγξ (λύζω) a spasmodic affection of the throat, hiccough, hiccup, λ. κενή an ineffectual retching, nothing being thrown off the stomach, Thuc.

λυγοσ.def: λῠ́γος, ἡ, vitex agnus castus, a willow-like tree, withy; in pl. its withes, Lat. vimina, Hom., Eur.

λυγοτευχησ.def: λῠγο-τευχής, ές (τεύχω) made of withes, Anth.

λυγροσ.def: λυγρός, ή, όν I. sore, baneful, mournful, Hom., Trag.: —τὰ λυγρά bane, misery, ruin, Hom., Hes. 2. baneful, with an act. force, φάρμακα λυγρά Od.; γαστὴρ λυγρή the stomach that cause of bane, id. 3. εἵματα λυγρά sorry garments, id. II. of persons, baneful, mischievous, id.: sorry, i. e. weak, cowardly, Hom., Soph. III. adv. -ρῶς, sorely, Il.

λυδια.def: Λῡδία, ἡ, Lydia, in Asia Minor, Hdt.

λυδιακα.def: Λυδιακά τὰ, Λυδιακά, a history of Lydia by Xanthus.

λυδιζω.def: Λῡδίζω, to play the Lydian, of Magnes, in reference to his play called Λυδοί, Ar.

λυδιοσ.def: Λύδιος, η, ον of Lydia, Lydian, Pind., etc.: —Λυδία λίθος, a stone used to assay gold, Soph.; also, Λ. πέτρα Theocr.

λυδιστι.gloss: in the Lydian tongue, after the Lydian fashion
λυδιστι.def: Λυδιστί in the Lydian tongue, after the Lydian fashion, Plat.: of Music, in the Lydian mode, ἡ Λ. ἁρμονία id.

λυδοσ.def: Λῡδός, οῦ, a Lydian, Pind., Hdt., etc.

λυζω.def: λύζω, to have the hiccough or hiccup, to sob violently, Ar., Anth. (Formed from the sound.)

λυη.def: λύη, δοριξ λύα, ἡ, (λύω) dissolution: hence, faction, sedition, Pind.

λυθρον.def: λύθρον, ου, τό, (λούω) defilement from blood, gore, Hom., Anth.

λυθρωδησ.def: λυθρ-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) defiled with gore, Anth.

λυκαβασ.def: λῠκ̆ά-βας, αντος, (Prob. from ⁎λύκη, βαίνω, the path of light, the sun's course.) I. a year, Od., Bion. II. λῠκᾰβαντίδες, ὧραι, ῶν, αἱ, the hours that make up the year, Anth.

λυκαινα.def: λῠ́καινα, ἡ, (fem. of λύκος,) a she-wolf, Babr., Plut.

λυκαιοσ.def: Λῠκαῖος, η, ον I. Lycaean, Arcadian, Epith. of Zeus, Hdt., Pind., etc. II. Λύκαιον, ου, his temple, Plut.; so, Λ. σήκωμα Eur. 2. Mount Lycaeus in Arcadia, Theocr. III. Λύκαια, sc. ἱερά, τά, the festival of Lycaean Zeus, Xen.:—also = Roman Lupercalia, Plut.

λυκαονια.def: Λυκαονία, ἡ, a district in the S. of Asia Minor, Xen., etc.: the people were Λυκάονες, οἱ, id.:—adv. Λυκιστί, in Lycaonian, NTest.

λυκαυγησ.def: λῠκ-αυγής, ές (⁎λύκη, αὐγή) of or at twilight: τὸ λυκαυγές early dawn, Luc.

λυκειον.def: λύκειον the Lyceum, a gymnasium with covered walks in the Eastern suburb of Athens, named after the neighbouring temple of Apollo Λύκειος, Ar., Plat., etc.

λυκειοσ.def: λῠ́κειος, ον I. of or belonging to a wolf, Eur. II. Λύκειος, as epith. of Apollo, either as λυκοκτόνος (q. v.), or as the Lycian god (v. Λυκηγενής), or (from ⁎λύκη) as the god of light, Aesch.; there is a play upon the doubtful meanings, Λύκει’ ἄναξ, λύκειος γενοῦ στρατῷ δαΐῳ, Lycean lord, be a very wolf to the enemy, id.

λυκη.def: λύκη light, a Root, whence come λυκά-βας, λύχνος, etc.

λυκηγενησ.def: Λῠκη-γενής, ές (γίγνομαι) of Apollo, commonly explained Lycian-born, i. e. at Patara, Il.

λυκιαρχησ.def: Λῠκι-άρχης, ου, ὁ, (ἄρχω) president of the Lycians, Strab.

λυκιδευσ.def: λῠκῐδεύς, έως, (λύκος) a wolf's whelp, Solon., Theocr.

λυκιοεργησ.def: Λυκιοεργής of Lycian workmanship, Hdt., Dem.

λυκιοι.def: Λύκιοι, οἱ, I. the Lycians, Il., etc. II. epith. of Apollo (cf. Λύκειος), Pind., Eur.

λυκοθαρσησ.def: λῠκο-θαρσής, ές (θάρσος) bold as a wolf, Anth.

λυκοκτονοσ.def: λῠκο-κτόνος, ὁ, (κτείνω) epith. of Apollo, wolf-slayer, Soph.

λυκοσ.def: λῠ́κος, ὁ, Lat. lupus, a wolf, Hom.;—proverb., λύκον ἰδεῖν to see a wolf, i. e. to be struck dumb, as was vulgarly believed of any one of whom a wolf got the first look, Plat., Theocr. (so Virg., Moerim lupi videre priores); λύκος οἶν ὑμεναιοῖ, of an impossibility, Ar.

λυκοφωσ.def: λῠκό-φως, ωτος, (⁎λύκη) twilight, the gloaming, Lat. diluculum.

λυκοω.def: λῠκόω, (λύκος) to tear like a wolf:—Pass. to be torn by wolves, πρόβατα λελυκωμένα Xen.

λυμα.gloss: the water used in washing, washings, off-scourings, filth
λυμα.def: λῦμα, ατος, εος, (λούω) I. mostly in pl. the water used in washing, washings, off-scourings, filth, Il.; λύμαθ’ ἁγνίσας ἐμά, of blood on the hands, Soph. II. moral filth, defilement, in sg., id. III. = λύμη, ruin, bane, Aesch.; of a person, λῦμα Ἀχαιῶν, i. e. Hector, Eur.

λυμαινομαι.gloss: to treat with indignity, to outrage, to maltreat
λυμαινομαι.def: λυμαίνομαι (λύμη) I. to treat with indignity, to outrage, to maltreat, c. acc., Hdt., Soph., etc.; c. acc. cogn., λύμης, ἥν με ἐλυμήνω Eur.:—of things, τὰς ῥήσεις ἃς ἐλυμαίνου the speeches you used to murder (as an actor), Dem.; ὀψοποιία λ. τὰ ὄψα spoils, Xen. 2. c. dat. to inflict indignities or outrages upon, Hdt., Ar., etc. 3. absol. to cause ruin, Thuc., Xen. II. sometimes as Pass., λυμανθὲν δέμας Aesch.; λελυμάνθαι Dem.

λυμαντηρ.def: λῡμαντήρ, ῆρος, a spoiler, destroyer, Xen.

λυμαντηριοσ.def: λυμαντήριος injurious, destructive, Aesch.: c. gen. destroying, ruining, id.

λυμαντησ.def: λυμαντής, οῦ, as adj. ruining, c. gen., Soph.

λυμεων.def: λῡμεών, ῶνος, (λύμη) a destroyer, spoiler, corrupter, Soph., Eur.

λυμη.def: λῡ́μη, ἡ, I. brutal outrage, maltreatment, maiming, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—in pl. outrages, indignities, Hdt., Aesch. II. = λῦμα, defilement, Polyb.

λυπεω.gloss: to give pain to, to pain, distress, grieve, vex, annoy
λυπεω.def: λυπέω I. to give pain to, to pain, distress, grieve, vex, annoy, Hdt., Trag., etc.; ἡ θώραξ λ. distresses by its weight, Xen.:—absol. to cause pain or grief, Soph. 2. of marauders, to harass, annoy by constant attacks, Hdt., Thuc., etc. II. Pass. with fut. mid. to be pained, grieved, distressed, Theogn., etc.; μὴ λυπέεο be not distressed, Hdt.:—c. acc. cogn., λύπας λυπεῖσθαι Plat.:—also c. acc. rei, to grieve about a thing, Soph.:—absol. to feel pain, Eur., etc.

λυπη.def: λῡ́πη, ἡ, 1. pain of body, Lat. dolor, Plat.: distress, sad plight or condition, Hdt. 2. pain of mind, grief, id., attic.

λυπηροσ.def: λῡπηρός, ή, όν (λυπέω) I. of things, painful, distressing, Lat. molestus, Hdt., attic II. of persons, 1. in good sense, causing sorrow by one's departure, Eur. 2. in bad sense, causing pain, troublesome, vexatious, offensive, Soph., Thuc., etc. III. adv. λυπηρῶς, painfully, so as to cause pain, Soph.; λυπηρῶς ἔχει it is painful, id.

λυπητεοσ.def: λῡπητέος, ον (verb. adj.) one must feel pain, Xen.

λυπροβιοσ.def: λυπρό-βιος, ον leading a wretched life.

λυπροσ.def: λυπρός, ή, όν (λυπέω) I. wretched, poor, sorry, of land, Od., Hdt. II. of persons, causing pain, offensive, troublesome, Aesch., Eur. 2. of states and conditions, painful, distressing, Aesch., Eur. III. adv., λυπρῶς ἔφερεν, aegre ferebat, Eur.

λυπροτησ.def: λυπρότης, ητος, poverty, of land, Strab.

λυπροχωροσ.def: λυπρό-χωρος, ον (χώρα) with poor land, Strab.

λυρα.def: λῠ́ρα, ἡ, Lat. lyra, a lyre, a Greek musical instrument like the κιθάρα, invented by Hermes, with seven strings, Hhymn., Eur.

λυραοιδοσ.gloss: one who sings to the lyre
λυραοιδοσ.def: λῠρ-αοιδός, οῦ, ὁ, one who sings to the lyre, Anth.:— contr. λυρῳδός, id., Plut.

λυριζω.def: λῠρίζω, (λύρα) to play the lyre, Anacreont.

λυρικοσ.def: λῠρικός, ή, όν I. of or for the lyre, lyric, Anacreont. II. as Subst., a lyrist, Anth., Plut.

λυριον.def: λύριον, ου, τό, (Dim. of λύρα, Ar.)

λυρογηθησ.def: λῠρο-γηθής, ές (γηθέω) delighting in the lyre, Anth.

λυροεισ.def: λῠρόεις, εσσα, εν (λύρα) fitted for the lyre, lyric, Anth.

λυροθελγησ.def: λῠρο-θελγής, ές (θέλγω) charmed by the lyre, Anth.

λυροκτυπια.def: λῠροκτῠπία, ἡ, a striking the lyre, Anth. (from λῠροκτῠπος)

λυροποιικοσ.def: λῠροποιικός, ή, όν (= λυροποιητικός) ἡ -κή, sc. τέχνη, the art or craft of lyre-making, Plat. (from λῠροποιός)

λυροποιοσ.def: λῠρο-ποιός, οῦ, ὁ, (ποιέω) a lyre-maker, Plat.

λυσανδρια.gloss: a festival in honour of Lysander
λυσανδρια.def: Λυσάνδρια, ων, τά, a festival in honour of Lysander, Plut.

λυσανιησ.def: λῡς-ᾰνίης, ου, ὁ, (ἀνία) ending sorrow, Ar.

λυσιζωνοσ.def: λῡσί-ζωνος, ον (ζώνη) loosing the zone, epith. of Eileithyia, who assisted women in travail, Theocr.

λυσιμαχοσ.def: λῡσί-μᾰχος, ον (μάχη) ending strife, Anth.: fem. λυσιμάχη, Ar.

λυσιμελησ.def: λῡσι-μελής, ές (μέλος) limb-relaxing, of sleep, etc., Od., Hes., etc.

λυσιμεριμνοσ.def: λῡσι-μέριμνος, ον (μέριμνα) driving care away, Anth.

λυσιμοσ.def: λῠ́σῐμος, ον I. able to loose or relieve, Aesch. II. pass. that can be redeemed, redeemable, Plat.

λυσιοσ.def: λῠ́σιος, η, ον (λύσις) releasing, delivering, Plat.

λυσιπαιγμων.def: λῠσῐ-παίγμων, ον, (παῖγμα) giving a loose to play or sport, Anacreont.

λυσιποθοσ.def: λῡσί-ποθος, ον delivering from love, Anth.

λυσιπονοσ.def: λῡσί-πονος, ον releasing from toil, Pind.

λυσισ.gloss: a loosing, setting free, releasing, ransoming
λυσισ.def: λῠ́σις, γεν. εως ιονιξ ιος, ἡ, (λύω) I. a loosing, setting free, releasing, ransoming, of a slain man, Il.; λ. θανάτου deliverance from death, Od.; πενίης Theogn., etc. 2. absol. a means of letting loose, Soph.:— deliverance from guilt by expiatory rites, id.; οὐδ’ ἔχει λύσιν [τὰ πήματα] admit not of atonement, id. II. a loosing, parting, λ. ψυχῆς ἀπὸ σώματος Plat.:— dissolution, πολιτείας Arist. III. = δόρπου λ. a place for banqueting, Pind.

λυσιτελεω.def: λῡσιτελέω, (= λύω, τέλη, v. λύω V) I. to pay what is due, and then "to pay, " i. e. to profit, avail, c. dat., λυσιτελεῖ τί τινι Ar., Plat.:—impers., λυσιτελεῖ μοι it profits me, is better for me, τεθνάναι λυσιτελεῖ ἢ ζῆν 'tis better to be dead than alive, Andoc.; λυσιτελεῖ μοι ὥσπερ ἔχω ἔχειν it is expedient for me to be as I am, Plat. II. neut. part. as Subst., τὸ λυσιτελοῦν, profit, gain, advantage, id., Dem.; τὰ λυσιτελοῦντα Thuc. (from λῡσιτελής)

λυσιτελησ.def: λῡσι-τελής, ές (λύω V, τέλος) 1. paying what is due: hence, useful, profitable, advantageous, Plat.; τὸ λυσιτελέστατον πρὸς ἀργύριον what was most profitable in point of money, Dem. 2. cheap, Xen.

λυσιτελουντωσ.def: λυσιτελούντως (part. pres. of λυσιτελέω,) usefully, profitably, Xen.

λυσιφλεβησ.def: λῡσι-φλεβής, ές (φλέψ) opening the veins, Anth.

λυσιφρων.def: λῡσί-φρων, ονος, (φρήν) releasing from care, Anacreont.

λυσιωδοσ.gloss: one who played women's characters in male attire
λυσιωδοσ.def: λυσι-ῳδός, οῦ, ὁ, one who played women's characters in male attire, Plut.

λυσσα.def: λύσσα, αττιξ λύττα, ἡ, I. rage, fury, esp. martial rage, Il. 2. after Hom. raging madness, raving, frenzy, Trag. II. canine madness, rabies, Xen.

λυσσαινω.def: λυσσαίνω, to rave, τινί against one, Soph.

λυσσαω.def: λυσσάω, (λύσσα) I. to be raging in battle, Hdt. 2. to rave, be mad, Soph., Plat. II. of dogs, Ar.; of wolves, Theocr.

λυσσημα.def: λύσσημα, ατος, εος, (from λυσσάω) a fit of madness: in pl. ravings, Eur.

λυσσητηρ.def: λυσσητήρ one that is raging or raving mad, Il., Anth.

λυσσοω.def: λυσσόω, (λύσσα) to enrage, madden, epic part. λυσσώων, Anth.

λυσσωδησ.def: λυσς-ώδης, ες (εἶδος) 1. like one raging, frantic, of martial rage, Il. 2. of madness, Soph., Eur.

λυτεοσ.def: λῠτέος, ον (verb. adj. of λύω,) one must solve, Plat.

λυτηρ.def: λῠτήρ, ῆρος, (λύω) I. one who looses, a deliverer, Eur. II. an arbitrator, decider, νεικέων Aesch.

λυτηριοσ.def: λῠτήριος, ον (λύω) I. loosing, releasing, delivering, Aesch.:—c. gen., τῶνδ’ ἐμοὶ λυτήριος my deliverer from these things, id.; ἐκ θανάτου λ. Eur. II. = λύτρον, recompense, Pind.

λυτικοσ.def: λῠτικός, ή, όν (λύω) refutative, of arguments, Arist.

λυτοσ.def: λῠτός, ή, όν (λύω) I. that may be loosed or dissolved, Plat. II. of arguments, refutable, Arist.

λυτρον.def: λύτρον, ου, τό, (λύω) a price paid, 1. for ransom, a ransom, mostly in pl. ransom-money, Hdt.; λύτρα λαβεῖν τινος to receive as ransom for.., Thuc.; λύτρα ἀποδιδόναι, καταθεῖναι to pay ransom, Dem. 2. an atonement, συμφορᾶς for calamity, Pind.; in pl., Plat.; so also, λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν NTest. 3. generally, a recompense, Pind.

λυτροω.gloss: to release on receipt of ransom, to hold to ransom
λυτροω.def: λυτρόω (λύτρον) to release on receipt of ransom, to hold to ransom, Plat.:—Pass. to be ransomed, Dem.

λυτρωσισ.def: λύτρωσις, ιος I. ransoming, Plut. II. redemption.

λυτρωτεοσ.def: λυτρωτέος, ον (verb. adj. of λυτρόω,) one must ransom, Arist.

λυτρωτησ.def: λυτρωτής, οῦ, (λυτρόω) a ransomer, redeemer, NTest.

λυχνεων.gloss: a place to keep lamps in
λυχνεων.def: λυχνεών, ῶνος, (λύχνος) a place to keep lamps in, Luc.

λυχνιον.def: λυχνίον, ου, τό, (λύχνος) a lamp-stand, Theocr., Luc.

λυχνισ.def: λυχνίς, ίδος (λύχνος) I. lychnis, a plant with a scarlet flower, Anth. II. a precious stone that emits light, prob. the ruby, Luc.

λυχνισκοσ.def: λυχνίσκος, ὁ, a kind of fish, Luc.

λυχνιτησ.gloss: a precious stone of a red colour
λυχνιτησ.def: λυχνῑ́της, ου, ὁ, (λύχνος) a precious stone of a red colour, Strab.

λυχνοκαια.gloss: a lighting of lamps, feast of Lanterns
λυχνοκαια.def: λυχνο-καΐα, ιονιξ -ΐη, ἡ, (καίω) a lighting of lamps, feast of Lanterns, Hdt.

λυχνοποιοσ.def: λυχνο-ποιός, όν (ποιέω) making lamps or lanterns, Ar.

λυχνοπολισ.def: λυχνό-πολις, ιος city of lamps, Luc.

λυχνοπωλησ.def: λυχνο-πώλης, ου, ὁ, (πωλέω) a dealer in lamps or lanterns, Ar.

λυχνοσ.def: λύχνος, ὁ, 1. pl. λύχνοι and λύχνα: — a portable light, a lamp, carried in the hand or set on a lamp-stand (λυχνίον), Od., Hdt., attic; περὶ λύχνων ἁφάς about lamplighting time, Hdt. 2. in pl. the lamp-market, Ar.

λυχνοφοροσ.def: λυχνο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) carrying a lamp, Plut.

λυω.def: λύω (Dep.) Orig. sense, to loose: I. of things, to loosen, unbind, unfasten, ζωστῆρα, θώρηκα Il.; ἀσκὸν λ. to untie a skin (used as a bottle), Od.; λ. ἡνίαν to slack the rein, Soph.; λ. γράμματα to open a letter, Eur.; στόμα λ. to open the mouth, id.; λ. ὀφρύν to unfold the brow, id., etc.:—Mid., ἐλύσατο ἱμάντα undid her belt, Il.; λύσασθαι τρίχα to unbind one's hair, Bion. 2. of living beings, a. of horses, etc., to undo, unyoke, unharness, Hom.; Mid., λύεσθαι ἵππους ὑπ’ ὄχεσφι to unyoke one's horses, Il. b. of men, to loose, release from bonds or prison, from difficulty or danger, Hom., Att:—Mid. to get one loosed or set free, Hes. c. of prisoners, to release on receipt of ransom (ἄποινα), hold to ransom, release, Hom.; λύειν τινὰ ἀποίνων on payment of ransom, Il.:—Mid. to release by payment of ransom, to get a person released, to ransom, redeem, Hom., attic 3. to give up, [θρόνον] λῦσον ἄμμιν Pind. II. to resolve a whole into its parts, to dissolve, break up, λ. ἀγορήν to dissolve the assembly, Hom.; also to break up the market, Xen.:— Pass., λῦτο ἀγών Il.; ἐλύθη ἡ στρατιά Xen. 2. to loosen, slacken, σπάρτα λέλυνται, i. e. have rotted, Il. 3. to loosen, i. e. weaken, relax, λῦσέ οἱ γυῖα made his limbs slack or loose, i. e. killed him, id.; λ. μένος τινί id.; but, καμάτωι γούνατ’ ἔλυσαν made the knees weak with toil, Od.:—so in Pass., λύντο δὲ γυῖα, as the effect of death, sleep, weariness, fear, etc., Il., etc.; γυῖα λέλυντο Hom., etc. 4. to undo, bring to naught, break down, destroy, Hom.: and generally, to undo, do away with, put an end to, Lat. dissolvere, id., attic; λ. βίον, i. e. to die, Eur. b. to repeal, annul, do away with, Hdt., etc.; λ. ψῆφον to rescind a vote, Dem.:— Pass., λέλυται πάντα all ties are broken, id. c. to solve a problem or difficulty, Plat. d. to refute an argument, Arist. e. to unravel the plot of a tragedy, id. 5. to break a law or treaty, Hdt., Thuc. III. to solve, fulfil, accomplish, τὰ μαντεῖα Soph. IV. to atone for, make up for, Lat. luere, id., Eur. V. μισθοὺς λύειν to pay wages in full, Xen. 2. τέλη λύειν λυσιτελεῖν, to pay, profit, avail, ἔνθα μὴ τέλη λύει φρονοῦντι where it boots not to be wise, Soph.; also λύει alone, much like λυσιτελεῖ, λύει ἄλγος Eur.; φημὶ τοιούτους γάμους λύειν βροτοῖς id.

λωβαομαι.gloss: to treat despitefully, to outrage, maltreat
λωβαομαι.def: λωβάομαι (Dep.) (λώβη) I. to treat despitefully, to outrage, maltreat, λώβην λωβᾶσθαί τινα to do one despite, Il.: esp. to maim, mutilate, Hdt.; λ. βίον to make ruin of one's life, Soph.; λ. τοὺς νέους to corrupt the youth, Plat.:—sometimes, like λυμαίνομαι, c. dat., Ar., Plat.:—absol. to do despite, act outrageously, Il. II. the perf. is used in pass. sense, λελωβημένος mutilated, Hdt., Plat.; also aor1 pass., μεγάλας λώβας λωβηθείς Plat.

λωβευω.gloss: to mock, make a mock of
λωβευω.def: λωβεύω, to mock, make a mock of, τινά Od. (from λώβη)

λωβη.def: λώβη, ἡ, 1. despiteful treatment, outrage, dishonour, Hom., Hdt., attic:—esp. mutilation, maiming, Hdt. 2. of persons, a disgrace, Lat. opprobrium, λώβην εἶναι Il.

λωβητηρ.gloss: one who treats despitefully, a foul slanderer
λωβητηρ.def: λωβητήρ, ῆρος, I. one who treats despitefully, a foul slanderer, Il.; a destroyer, of the Furies, Soph. II. pass. a worthless wretch, Il.

λωβητησ.def: λωβητής, οῦ, (= λωβητήρ) λ. τέχνης one who disgraces his trade, Ar.

λωβητοσ.def: λωβητός, ή, όν (λωβάομαι) I. despitefully treated, outraged, Il., Soph. II. act. insulting, abusive, Soph.

λωιων.def: λωίων, ονος, (from λάω 2, λῶ) I. more desirable, more agreeable, and (generally) better, τόδε λώιόν ἐστι Hom.; and as adv. better, Od.:—we also find a comp. λωΐτερος, ον, in neut., λωίτερον καὶ ἄμεινον id.—In attic λῴων was used as comp. of ἀγαθός. II. Sup. λῷστος, η, ον Theogn., attic; τὰ λῷστα βουλεύειν Aesch.; ὦ λῷστε my good friend, Plat.

λωμα.def: λῶμα, ατος, εος, the border of a robe:—Dim. λωμάτιον, τό, Anth.

λωοσ.def: λῷος, ὁ, a Macedon. month, answering to the attic βοηδρομιών, Philipp. ap. Dem.

λωπη.def: λώπη, ἡ, (λέπω) a covering, robe, mantle, Od., Theocr.

λωποδυτεω.def: λωποδῠτέω, I. to steal clothes, esp. from bathers or travellers, Plat., Xen. II. generally, to rob, plunder, Ar. (from λωποδῠ́της)

λωποδυτησ.gloss: one who slips into another's clothes, a clothes-stealer
λωποδυτησ.def: λωπο-δῠ́της, ου, ὁ, (λῶπος, δύω) I. one who slips into another's clothes, a clothes-stealer, esp. one who steals the clothes of bathers, or strips travellers, Soph. II. generally, a thief, robber, footpad, Ar., Dem.

λωτιζομαι.gloss: to choose for oneself, cull the best
λωτιζομαι.def: λωτίζομαι, (λῶτος) Mid. to choose for oneself, cull the best, Aesch.

λωτινοσ.def: λώτῐνος, η, ον (λωτός) made of lotus-wood, Theocr.

λωτισμα.def: λώτισμα, ατος, εος, a flower: metaph. the fairest, choicest, best, Eur.

λωτοεισ.def: λωτόεις, εσσα, εν overgrown with lotus, πεδία λωτεῦντα (ionic for -όεντα) lotus-plains, Il.

λωτοσ.def: λωτός, οῦ, the lotus, name of several plants. I. the Greek lotus, a plant on which horses fed, a kind of clover or trefoil, Hom. II. the Cyrenean lotus, an African shrub, whose fruit was the food of certain tribes on the coast, hence called Lotophagi, Od., Hdt. III. the Egyptian lotus, the lily of the Nile, Hdt. IV. a North-African tree; from its hard black wood flutes were made:—hence Λιβὺς λωτός is used in Poets for a flute, Eur.

λωτοτροφοσ.def: λωτο-τρόφος, ον (λωτός I) producing lotus, Eur.

λωτοφαγοι.def: λωτο-φάγοι, οἱ, (λωτός II) the Lotus-eaters, a peaceful people on the coast of Cyrenaica, Od., Hdt.

λωφαω.gloss: to rest from toil, take rest
λωφαω.def: λωφάω, I. to rest from toil, take rest, Il. 2. c. gen. to take rest or abate from, recover from, χόλου Aesch.; πόνου Soph.; λ. ἀπὸ νόσου καὶ πολέμου Thuc. 3. to abate, of a disease, id. II. trans. to lighten, relieve, ὁ λωφήσων γὰρ οὐ πέφυκέ πω Aesch. (deriv. uncertain)

λωφηιοσ.def: λωφήιος, η, ον (from λωφάω) relieving, λ. ἱερά expiatory offerings, Apoll.
